"No," the boy lied.

"When the Eaters lived and skirred the stars, they visited the worlds of a thousand thousand different beings, and those beings likewise visited our own world. Several of those beings had assembled a coven that spanned the firmament, and they welcomed the Eaters into its fold. For ages the civilizations of the coven knew kindness and prosperity, and to all reaches of the clustered cosmos did the domain of the coven stretch. One of the beings of the coven hailed from a faraway and darkling star. With Its mind It could fold the fabric of space and time as you or I might fold a supper cloth. To the coven It was known as Ptoh."

"For reasons we can but fathom the civilizations of the stars indicted Ptoh. It was the will of the coven that It be held on our very world in the bondage of the Eaters. They contrived for Ptoh a prison from which It could not fold Itself away, and there Ptoh languished for eons. In time, the Eaters left or perished, and the coven was forgotten to our world. Yet here Ptoh remains imprisoned."

"And what of the black prism?" asked the boy.
translation:

“出于我们只能猜测的原因，群星诸文明起诉了 普托。

source:
"A handful of black sand, drawn from the shores of a dreary rock that spun about Ptoh's star. The sands were fired in the burning gases of that star and cooled suddenly when Ptoh appeared in Qud a moment thence. It is said that Ptoh bestowed the glass to an ancient custodian of Its prison so that the man might free It. Once the man had chosen to wield the glass, it began to mantle with an amaranthine hue. You see, those that peer through its faces are given to fits of madness, for they see the world by the light of Ptoh's star, and they see themselves as Ptoh does."

"What will become of it? Does it frighten you?"

"Immensely. I mean to see it destroyed. But it bears the properties of no earthly glass, and my guild would never forgive me if I forsook the chance to study it first. It was the jewelers who bartered the thing from Priam's grieving sister. Now, enough of this splendor. You are to study still." Uri lifted another stone. "Hmm?"

But the boy's eyes stayed fixed on the prism.

{{W|Author's Foreward}}

I initially had no intention of writing any of this down. What business is it of mine, I thought, to divest the ignorant of their hard-earned bliss? Who am I to speak up against the static inertia of incurious dullards who choose to cultivate their lack of awareness of the world around them as my witless kin tend to their tidy watervine rows? I am a warrior, scientist, and chef; devoting my time to educating the undeserving is the least of my many desires. After enough time spent among other alleged sentients, however, I determined that more of my time has been wasted in correcting so-called 'experts' concerning this matter than I would waste by writing a text about it.

So: here. You're welcome.


Chef Agate Severance Star

source:
The very core of hindren culture is an overwhelming fear that governs every facet of their being. They call outsiders 'kendren' and refuse to believe that they can be understood. They fear boars even as they cook and eat boar-flesh. They fear one another. But the most extraordinary incorporation of fear into the hindren way of life is, without a doubt, the cultivation of fear. I refer not to the Hindriarch's propaganda or proliferation of fear-mongering tall tales, though both are mainstays of Bey Lah; I refer specifically to the taming and cultivation of the lah plant, whose alpha and omega of life are steeped in blood and fear.

It is here that I debunk the most common misconception concerning lah: that the dreadroot is a separate entity. It is not. The dreadroot is the protruding stem of the lah rhizome, doing its very most to survive until it can blossom into the lahbloom as it does in the flower fields.
      
I have wasted unforgivable amounts of time and energy explaining the connection between these two life phases of the same plant to the ignorant. Usually, they will point out that dreadroot grows all throughout Qud's southwest canyons, but it is exceedingly rare to discover feral lah there. To this I reply: if, after whatever studies you claim to have made, you are yet incapable of deciphering the workings of even the most basic ecosystems, I cannot help you. For those of you who are capable of basic logic and adjustment of personal worldview, please read on.

In spite of being a 'flowering' plant, lah is not a true flower, its 'blooms' not true blossoms. Lah is a root with a decorative upper stem, reproducing through the distribution of rhizomes. The baboons and snapjaws of the canyons use the dreadroot supply for food and love the taste of its petals, and any root unfortunate enough to bloom will quickly be defoliated by hungry mammals. Though dreadroot is capable of inducing fear, any relatively intelligent creature is able to overcome the fearful association to return and eat. The process being what it is, fragments of dreadroot are distributed, the rhizome takes root, and dreadroot proliferates without thriving. So it goes.
      
In the flower fields, however, the varied nature of both predators and available food changes. Boars seek a varied diet mainly consisting of starapples and reptiles, not showing a particular interest in dreadroot or lah. The boars will eat lah if no better food is available, but it's quite unusual for such scarcity to disrupt boar territories. Thus: lah flourishes, gaining a measure of cognitive process, limited mobility, and a new means of reproduction.

On reproduction: another common misconception is that feral lah attacks because it is hungry. It is not. Feral lah's practical lifespan is short; it is rare for a fully-grown bloom to survive longer than a week -- and during that time it subsists completely on water, salt sun, and soil. The advantage of lah's murderous demeanor is not to sustain itself, but to dramatically speed reproduction of its kind.
      
Most of a lah blossom's growing energy goes into making its 'tumbling pods', thorn-covered husks possessed of tremendous kinetic tension. Through violent shifting of the rhizome's weight inside, these husks roll along the ground at high speed until they encounter a living creature. They then release the surface tension of their husks and detonate, flinging flesh-piercing thorns and buds all around, just after making an obnoxious squeaking noise. If the prey is killed, the rhizome buds can then take nutrients from the prey's corpse and quickly grow into a new feral lah plant.

There is no textual 'proof' to present to those who still believe that dreadroot and lah are different plants, but I happily invite skeptical parties to babysit a dreadroot and defend it from baboons until it matures, an endeavor that will take about as much time as you have removed from the end of my life through the stress of listening to your absurd demands.

Any hindren pariah you meet will have seen dreadroot mature into lah countless times. Go bother one of them.
      
For those who are more interested in the culinary applications of lah in all of its life cycles than said life cycles themselves, I soon plan to release {{g|The Blood and Fear Cookbook}}, a collection of recipes that, from feral leaf crudites to petalsteaks, elevate one of Qud's more interesting plants to a level far beyond the bland mah lah soup of my village of origin.
translation:
兴德伦 文化的核心，是一种压倒性的恐惧，支配
着他们存在的每个侧面。他们称外来者为“
肯德伦”，并拒绝相信外人能够理解他们。他们
害怕野猪，哪怕他们烹煮并食用野猪肉。他们也害怕彼此。
但毫无疑问，兴德伦 生活方式中对恐惧最非凡的
吸纳，便是恐惧的栽培。我指的不是
兴德伦族长 的宣传，也不是恐惧贩子式荒诞故
事的扩散，尽管二者都是 贝拉赫 的支
柱；我特指对 拉赫 植物的驯化与种植，其生命的始与终
都浸透血与恐惧。
我在这里驳斥关于 拉赫 最常见的误解：恐根是一个独立
实体。它不是。恐根是 拉赫 根茎突出的茎部，正竭尽全
力存活，直到它能像在
花田中那样绽放为 拉赫 花。
我已经浪费了不可饶恕的大量时间与精力，向无知者解释
同一植物这两个生命阶段之间的联系。通常，他们会指出
恐根遍布 库德 西南峡谷，但在那里发现野生 拉赫 却极
其罕见。对此我的回答是：倘若在你自称完成了无论什么
研究之后，仍无法解读哪怕最基础生态系统的运作，我帮
不了你。至于你们当中具备基本逻辑，并能调整个人世界
观的人，请继续读下去。
尽管 拉赫 是一种“开花”植物，它并不是真正的花，它
的“花朵”也不是真正的花。拉赫 是一种带装饰性上茎
的根，通过分布根茎来繁殖。峡谷中的狒狒和锯齿豺会把
恐根储备当作食物，也喜爱其花瓣的味道；任何不幸开花
的根都会很快被饥饿哺乳动物吃光叶片。尽管恐根能够诱
发恐惧，任何相对聪明的生物都能克服这种恐惧联想，回
来继续进食。过程就是这样：恐根碎片被分散，根茎扎根，
恐根扩散却并不兴盛。事情便如此。
然而，在花田中，捕食者与可用食物的多样性质都发生了
变化。野猪寻求多样食谱，主要由星苹果和爬行动物构成，
并不特别偏好恐根或 拉赫。如果没有更好的食物，野猪
会吃 拉赫，但这种食物匮乏扰乱野猪领地的情况相当少
见。因此：拉赫 繁盛起来，获得了一定程
度的认知过程、有限移动能力，以及新的繁殖方式。
关于繁殖：另一种常见误解是，野生 拉赫 攻击是因为饥
饿。并非如此。野生 拉赫 的实际寿命很短；完全长成的
花很少能活过一周，而在此期间，它完全依靠水、盐阳与
土壤维生。拉赫 那种杀戮性举止的优势并非维持自身，
而是显著加快同类繁殖。
一朵 拉赫 花的大部分生长能量都用于制造它的“翻滚荚”：
覆满尖刺、具有巨大动能张力的外壳。通过内部根茎重量
的剧烈转移，这些外壳会沿地面高速滚动，直到遇见活物。
随后，它们释放外壳的表面张力并爆裂，在刚发出恼人的
吱吱声后，把穿肉尖刺与芽体向四周抛射。若猎物被杀死，
根茎芽便能从猎物尸体中吸取养分，并快速长成新的野生
拉赫 植物。
没有文字“证据”可呈现给那些仍相信恐根与 拉赫 是不
同植物的人，但我很乐意邀请怀疑者去照看一
株恐根，并保护它免受狒狒侵扰直到成熟；这项工作所需
时间，大约等于我因聆听你们荒唐要求所受压力而从寿命
末端被削去的时间。
你遇到的任何 兴德伦 贱民都曾无数次见过恐根成
熟为 拉赫。去烦他们吧。
至于那些比起生命周期本身，更关心 拉赫 在其所有生命
周期中烹饪应用的人，我很快计划发布 {{g|《血与恐惧食谱》}}，
这是一套菜谱集，从野叶生蔬到花瓣排，将 库德 较有趣
的植物之一提升到远超我出身村庄那淡而无味的
玛赫 拉赫 汤的层次。

{{C|Translator's note: At a trashmoot in Taggamrod, piled under a mound of crushed and sticky glass, I found a pamphlet full of stories from the Shale Labyrinth. This one -- despite the mystifying absurdity of what it claims (or, perhaps, because of it) -- was the most extraordinary to me. Reader, do you agree?}}
      
{{y|She perched atop the branches of a blighted tree, staring up at the faint light of the spindle. When I spotted her, I caught myself mid-step, mid-breath, mid-thought. Have you ever known the misfortune of allowing your eyes to settle upon the divine vision of an apple farmer's daughter? If so, you understand how I felt in that moment.}}

Understand: I had done all I could, before now. I would have loved to stay elsewhere, but I'd traveled six parasangs with no rest, no discoveries but for a ruin occupied by an unfriendly cult. Too busy dodging arrows to ask about empty beds or compensation, I chose the apple farm instead. I took pains to avoid her when the salt sun shone, and so too did she avoid me, remaining a slight and swathed figure shying away in the periphery of my vision. I kept my focus on the farmer's craggy visage, on his wild and prominent whiskers, on his sweetly-rotting cider breath as we arranged the terms of my lodging.

It was not until the beetle moon passed overhead that I dared stand and wander, and it was then that I saw her, and the feeling of bone-deep infatuation at once seized me. I caught myself mid-step, mid-breath, mid-thought, and I stumbled onto a fallen twig. It snapped loudly. I stood still.

The beautiful creature atop the tree did not lift a finger or turn her head, but she did address me. "Moon and sun, traveler."

"Wisdom and will," I replied, gritting my teeth. It was a rare thing to hear the voice of an apple farmer's daughter, and it only seemed to increase the pressure on my racing hearts. I would not allow this all-encompassing feeling to overtake me. I longed for her to say something. I dreaded it.

A tense silence crawled by, until I gathered myself and broke it. "You're restless too?"
translation:
{{C|译者按：在 塔甘罗德 的一场垃圾集会上，我从
一堆破碎而黏腻的玻璃下翻出一本小册子，里面满是来自
页岩迷宫的故事。尽管这个故事的说法荒诞得令人费解（
或许也正因如此），它对我而言最为非凡。读者，你同意
吗？}}
      
{{y|她栖在一棵枯萎树的枝头，仰望纺锤微弱的光。我看见她
时，自己卡在半步、半息、半念之间。你可曾有过这样的
不幸：让双眼停驻在一位苹果农之女的神圣景象上？若有，
你便明白我那一刻的感受。}}
请理解：在此之前，我已尽力而为。我本愿住到别处，但
我已经走了
六帕拉桑格，未曾休息，也没有发现什么，除了一个由不
友善教团占据的废墟。我忙着躲箭，没空询问空床或报酬，
于是选择了苹果农场。盐阳照耀时，我费心避开她，而她
也同样避开我，只在我视野边缘保留一个纤细、裹缠、畏
缩的身影。我把注意力集中在农夫崎岖的面
容上，集中在他狂野而突出的胡须上，集中在我们商议住
宿条件时他那甜甜腐败的苹果酒气息上。
直到甲虫月从头顶经过，我才敢起身游荡；也正是在那时，
我看见了她，深入骨髓的迷恋立刻攫住我。我卡在半步、
半息、半念之间，踉跄踩上一根落枝。它啪地一声折断。
我僵立不动。
树上的美丽生灵没有抬一根手指，也没有转头，但她确实
对我开口。“月与日，旅人。”
“智慧与意志。”我咬紧牙关回答。听见苹果农之女的声
音是罕有之
事，而这似乎只让狂奔的心脏承受更大压力。我不会允许
这种包围一切的感觉吞没自己。我渴望她说些什么。我又
恐惧它。
紧绷的沉默缓缓爬过，直到我收束心神，将其打破。“你
也睡不安吗？”

She turned her head the barest degree toward mine. I still couldn't see her eyes. "Always," she replied, and I could hear the wry smirk in her voice.

"Does your father know you walk the orchard of a night?" I asked her.

"If you mean the apple farmer," she said, "he is not my father. We are family by choice. We always are, the farmers and the children."

I stared, gaping.

"I really ought not to have told you that," she continued, "but you seemed special, to resist the lure the way you're trying to do."

My jaw worked, but it took a few tries for my voice to catch up. "If what you say is true, then... what are you?" I managed at last.

"Already too candid." She kicked off the tree and landed gracefully with a flurry of her skirts. "I must take my leave."
translation:
她把头朝我这边转了极微小的一度。我仍看不见她的眼睛。
“一直都
是。”她回答，我能在她声音里听见狡黠的笑意。
“你父亲知道你夜里在果园散步吗？”我问她。
“如果你指的是那个苹果农，”她说，“他不是我的父亲。
我们是自愿选择的家人。农夫和孩子们一直都是这样。”
我瞪着她，张口结舌。
“我真的不该告诉你这个，”她继续说，“但你看起来很
特别，竟能像这样努力抵抗诱惑。”
我的下巴动了动，但试了几次，声音才终于跟上。“如果
你说的是真的，那么……你是什么？”我终于挤出这句话。
“已经太坦白了。”她蹬离树枝，裙摆翻飞，优雅落地。
“我必须告辞。”

"Wait!" My muscles clenched as she paused, considering. I pressed on. "Answer me this, at least: why apple farmers?"

She laughed, the beautiful tinkling crystal blade of her voice slicing my heart to ribbons. The last thing I heard before my faint consciousness surrendered its grasp on my mind was her trailing reply, receding with distance.

"Why, it's because we love starapples!"
translation:
“等等！”她停下斟酌时，我的肌肉绷紧。我继续追问。
“至少回答我这个：为什么是苹果农？”

她笑了，那美丽、叮当作响的水晶刀刃般嗓音把我的心切
成碎片。在我微弱的意识松开对心智的抓握之前，最后听
见的是她拖长的回答，随着距离远去。

“哎呀，因为我们爱星苹果呀！”

{{C|Editor's note: The following is an excerpt from the travel diary of Kaylenn Sand-Shell, who generously donated her leather-bound volumes to the Monastery of the Illustrious Heart of Chrome. May they remain forever preserved.}}
      
One can traverse the arable lands around Moghra'yi for lifetimes without ever encountering the deer-people who call themselves the 'hindren'. In numbers they are but a few hundred, and as a people they do not care to interact with other creatures when they can avoid it. In the twenty years I have actively wandered, I have met but a handful of wandering hindren families, all exiles from their home and yet unwilling to tell me how to find the society that made them pariahs.

I am, however, a hunter as well as a scholar, and after several years of searching I was able to locate their secret village, Bey Lah. All I will say of its location is that it is somewhere in the flower fields of Qud; I have no desire to betray the confidence of a mostly peaceful race of creatures.

My arrival was obviously not celebrated; the Meadow's border scouts are extremely perceptive and conversant in tracking and obfuscation alike. By changing landmarks, using confusing and threatening sounds, and otherwise making my stay in the adjacent wood as unpleasant as possible, they sought to deter me from my path while avoiding notice. When I eluded the guards and made my way to the first neat row of carefully-tended watervine, the hindren farmers who saw me at once took terrified flight.

The extreme of fear that hindren feel toward outsiders is a strange one, in my eyes. They are large, powerful creatures with arms and legs at least as strong as a human's and covered in dense fur that protects them from cold weather. Each individual is skilled at using and maintaining a sharp metal vinereaper. Their antlers are strong as bone and naturally quite sharp; hindren pariahs who learn to fight live longer than most of Qud's wayfarers.

Strange as this attitude may be to me, I cannot argue against its efficacy; the Bey Lah villagers have lived peacefully under informal matriarchal gerontocratic rule for generations. Their eldest or wisest woman becomes 'Hindriarch', and her word on most things is obeyed by every member of the tribe, who refer to her as 'Grand-doe'.

The current Hindriarch was the first hindren to hold a conversation with me, and I will admit to a measure of anxiety being under her hawkish gaze. She was none too pleased at my presence, but intelligent enough to understand that killing me or driving me away would be a greater inconvenience and danger than offering me hospitality. We parted with an uneasy compromise, and I began my residence and observation.

I found quickly that the oral history of the hindren is shoddy at best, perhaps with purpose. Their etymology is similarly muddy, but there are some observable patterns: 'Dren' is a suffix applied to sentients: 'hindren', obviously, and the word for their young, 'faundren'. I also heard 'kendren' a great deal, as it is their word for non-hostile sentients like myself. All hindren names end in the suffix 'hart' or 'hind'. Although they do understand that these are gendered terms (a majority of male fauns bear 'hind' names) it seems that for quite some time, 'hart' was a name appendage reserved for the smallest or most ill-behaved faundren. As it is, the suffixes are considered unisex in modern day, and the meadow's faundren now have a much more even distribution of the suffixes than their parents.

Life for hindren is, for the most part, uneventful to the point of what this traveler would consider extreme boredom. The watervine and lah fields are meticulously tended day after day, never harvested late and always producing as much crop as possible. Growing up, all faundren are trained as farmers, but a lucky few will become carpenters or blacksmiths in order to keep what little infrastructure they maintain running. Those who display particular aptitude and loyalty to the Hindriarch have a chance of becoming border scouts, who keep the nearby fields safe and occasionally bring in wild game or starapples while patrolling. The resulting side dishes provide some much needed variety from the daily Bey Lah staple, a hearty lah petal soup combined with crushed matz. While this 'mah lah soup' is delicious, I appreciated how the occasional serving of boar brisket gave a much needed spice to my day.

I found little else of interest from the adult hindren; they seemed unwilling to speak with me at length. While I heard rumors about a village treasure, I could not obtain any information about what that treasure actually might be.

By contrast, I learned a great deal speaking to the faundren, whose curiosity about the outside world is rapidly becoming difficult for the elders to contain. More than once I heard the term 'hartind', allegedly an ancient term for hindren who lived as both genders or neither, which the young ones take as evidence of a more egalitarian past. I can feel the wanderlust, both in their fascination with me and also in the zeal with which their elders would clamp down on any talk of lands outside of the meadows.

The world outside the flower fields remains an expanse of unavoidable peril for the adults of the tribe. Understandable, as Bey Lah trains few warriors. They have no standing military and only a handful of combat-trained scouts. The hindren take their border security rather seriously, and any of their number who chooses to leave does so permanently and is erased from the tribe's collective memory. The small families of hindren I met in the lah fields and, rarely, elsewhere in Qud, are all exiles, whether due to crimes committed or simply the choice to live elsewhere. Within Bey Lah itself, pariahs are even more thoroughly ostracized than I knew; any mention of their names is spoken only in whispers by the faundren, knowing that being caught speaking of the 'dead' means harsh punishment. This sits poorly with the young ones, and my instincts tell me that their dissatisfaction is a step beyond standard youthful rebellion; the winds of change are coming to Bey Lah.

By the time I left Bey Lah, it was with relief; I haven't the patience for the life these deer-people lead and I was beginning to catch cabin fever in spite of spending very little time in the village's brinestalk yurts. The Hindriarch was as happy to see me go as I was to be off; my pack was loaded with the vinewafers and dried flowers of which I'd long since grown tired and I was ushered out efficiently by scouts.

By the end of the day, I realized that I had taken something else: a faundren had snuck out of the settlement behind me and refused to return to their village. I hardened my heart against the faundren's pleas and found a scout to guide them back to town. If Resheph be merciful, the little one will find happiness there, or the luck to find a more fruitful life elsewhere. All I can say with certainty is that the poor thing does not lack for bravery.

{{C|编者按：以下摘自 凯伦 沙壳
的旅行日记。她慷慨地将自己的皮面卷册捐赠
给辉煌铬心修道院。愿它们永远得以保存。}}
一个人可以用数辈子穿行 莫格拉伊 周边的可耕
之地，却从未遇见那些自称“兴德伦”的鹿人。
他们数量不过数百，作
为一个族群，只要能避免，便不愿同其他生物互动。在我
积极游历的二十年里，我只遇见过寥寥几个流浪
兴德伦 家庭，他们全是被家园放逐者，却仍不愿
告诉我，该如何找到那个把他们变为贱民的社会。
不过，我既是猎人也是学者，经过数年搜寻，我终于找到
了他们秘密的村庄 贝拉赫。关于其位置，我只会说
它位于 库德 的某处花
田之中；我无意背叛一个大体和平种族对我的信任。
我的到来显然并未受到庆祝；草甸的边境斥候极为敏锐，
既精通追踪，也熟悉迷惑手段。他们通过改变
地标、使用混乱而威胁性的声音，以及其他一切尽可能让
我在邻近林地停留得不愉快的方式，试图在不被察觉的情
况下阻止我前进。当我避开守卫，来到第一排整齐且悉心
照料的水藤前时，看见我的 兴德伦 农民立刻惊恐
逃走。
在我看来，兴德伦 对外来者所感到的极端恐惧很
奇怪。他们是高大有力的生物，四肢至少和人类一样强壮，
身覆浓密毛皮，足以抵御寒冷天气。每个个体都擅长使用
和维护锋利的金属割藤器。他们的鹿角像骨头一样坚固，
且天然相当锐利；学会战斗的 兴德伦 贱民，比
库德 多数旅人都活得更久。
尽管这种态度对我而言很奇怪，我却无法否认它的效用；
贝拉赫 村民已经在非正式的母系长老统治下和平生
活了数代。他们最年长或最智慧的女性会成为“
兴德伦族长”，她对大多数事务的发言都会被
部族每个成员服从，而他们称她为“大母鹿”。
现任 兴德伦族长 是第一个同我交谈的
兴德伦，我承认，在她鹰隼般的注视下，我多少
有些焦虑。她对我的存在毫不高兴，但也足够聪明，明白
杀死我或赶走我，比接待我会带来更大的麻烦与危险。我
们以不安的妥协分开，而我开始居住并观察。
我很快发现，兴德伦 的口述历史充其量十分粗劣，
也许还是有意如此。他们的词源同样浑浊，但仍有一些可
观察模式：“德伦”是用于有知觉者的后缀：显然有
“兴德伦”，还有他们对幼者的称呼“
鹿民”。我也经常听到“肯德伦”，
这是他们称呼像我这样非敌对有知觉者的词。所有
兴德伦 名字都以“雄鹿”或“雌鹿”后
缀结尾。虽然他们确实明白这些是带性别的词（多数雄性
幼牧神使用“雌鹿”名），但似乎相当长一段时间里，
“雄鹿”是专为最小或最不守规矩的
鹿民 保留的名字附加词。如今，这些后缀在
现代被视为无
性别，草甸的 鹿民 现在比其父母一代更均匀
地分配这些后缀。
兴德伦 的生活大体上平淡无事，到了这名旅人会
称之为极端无聊的程度。水藤田和 拉赫 田日复一日被细
致照料，从不迟收，并总是尽可能产出最多作物。成长过
程中，所有 鹿民 都被训练为农民，但少数幸
运者会成为木匠或铁匠，以维持他们那点基础设施运转。
那些表现出特殊能力且忠于 兴德伦族长 的人，
有机会成为边境斥候；他们保护附近田地安全，并偶尔在
巡逻时带回野味或星苹果。由此得来的配菜，为 贝
拉赫 每日主食提供了一些急需的变化；这种主食是一种
丰盛的 拉赫 花瓣汤，混合碾碎的无酵饼。虽然这道“
玛赫 拉赫 汤”很美味，但偶尔一份野猪胸肉给
我的一天带来的必要辛香，也令我感激。
成年 兴德伦 身上，我没发现多少其他有趣之处；
他们似乎不愿同我长谈。虽然我听到关于村庄宝物的传闻，
却无法取得任何关于那宝物究竟可能是什么的信息。
相比之下，同 鹿民 交谈让我学到了很多；他
们对外部世界的好奇正迅速变得难以被长者压制。我不止
一次听到“哈廷德”这个词，据称它是一个古老
词语，用于指称同时以两种性别生活、或不以任何性别生
活的 兴德伦，年轻者把它视作过去更加平等的证
据。我能感到那种远游欲，无论是在他们对我的着迷中，
还是在他们的长者压制任何关于草甸之外土地谈话时的热
切中。
对部族成年人而言，花田之外的世界仍是一片不可避免的
危险旷野。这可以理解，因为 贝拉赫 训练的战士很
少。他们没有常备军，只有少数受过战斗训练的斥候。
兴德伦 相当认真地对待边境安全，而任何选择离
开者都将永久离开，并从部族集体记忆中抹除。我在
拉赫 田中，以及偶尔在 库德 其他地方遇到的小型
兴德伦 家庭，全都是流亡者，无论是因犯罪，还
是仅仅选择生活在别处。在 贝拉赫 内部，贱民遭受
的排斥甚至比我所知更彻底；任何提及他们名字的行为，
都只会由 鹿民 用耳语完成，因为他们知道，
被抓到谈论“死者”意味着严厉惩罚。年轻者对此并不满
意，而我的直觉告诉我，他们的不满已经超出标准青春叛
逆一步；变革之风正吹向 贝拉赫。
当我离开 贝拉赫 时，我感到如释重负；我没有耐心
过这些鹿人的生活，尽管我在村中盐茎毡帐里待的时间很
少，却已经开始感到幽闭烦躁。兴德伦族长 看
见我离开时的高兴，正如我启程时的高兴；我的背包被塞
满我早已厌倦的藤饼和干花，而斥候们高效地将我送出。
到当天结束时，我意识到自己还带走了别的东西：一名
鹿民 偷偷跟在我身后离开聚落，并拒绝返回
村庄。我硬起心肠不理会那 鹿民 的恳求，找
了一名斥候将其带回镇上。若 雷谢夫 仁慈，这小
家伙会在那里找到幸福，或幸运地在别处找到更有成果的
生活。我唯一能确定的是，可怜的小东西并不缺乏勇气。

[[{{w|I.}}]]
      
Once, the Earthling peered across a vast ocean of sand and asked, "Why - across the clustered cosmos - are mollusk civilizations most common?"

Eta smiled in patience. "You speak mistakenly, but your mistake is cousin to truth. It's correct that when geonauts dredge fossils from the ribbon of endless earths, the shells of whelk-folk are so numerous as to appear prosaic. But their prevalence isn't owned to their dominance, only the calcium of their shells, which decomposes less quickly than the gelatin of their peers, and the silt of their watery hearths, which gathers in soft eddies and shrouds their remains like a bed cloak. Do well and abide this truth, Earthling: the present is but one vista to the past.
translation:
[[{{w|I.}}]]
      
有一次，地球人凝望一片辽阔沙海，问道：“为什么，在
群聚宇宙中，软体动物文明最为常见？”
伊塔 耐心地微笑。“你说错了，但你的错误是真理的近
亲。地航者从无尽大地之带中捞挖化石时，螺民的壳确实
多到显得平凡。但它们的普遍并非源于支配地位，只源于
壳中的钙；钙比同侪的胶质分解得更慢，也源于它们水生
炉灶中的淤泥；淤泥聚于柔缓涡流，像床罩一样覆住它们
的遗骸。好好记住这条真理吧，地球人：现在不过是通往
过去的一处远景。”

source:
[[{{w|II.}}]]

Once, the Earthling stared at a garden snail and asked, "Is consciousness real, or merely an illusion?"

Eta smiled in patience. "Imagine an autumn breeze unlatching an acorn from its branch and casting it into a river. Does the acorn fall to the left or right bank?"

The Earthling frowned. "If it landed in the river, then the answer is neither, or rather, the answer is in between."

Eta let a moment pass before continuing. "Take care not to erect prisons out of your words, Earthling, lest you confine yourself from enlightenment's reach."
translation:
[[{{w|II.}}]]

有一次，地球人盯着一只花园蜗牛，问道：“意识是真实
的，还是仅
仅一种幻觉？”
伊塔 耐心地微笑。“想象一阵秋风从枝头解下一颗橡子，
将它抛入河中。橡子落向左岸，还是右岸？”地球人皱眉。
“如果它落进河里，那答案就是两者都不是，或者更确切
地说，答案在两者之间。”
伊塔 等了一会儿才继续。“小心别用你的言语筑起监牢，
地球人，以免你把自己囚禁在启悟触及不到的地方。”

source:
[[{{w|III.}}]]

The Earthling held a ptychosaur bone in their hand and mused, "What poor creatures! They roamed their planet in sovereignty for millions of years, yet now only through their dusty skeletons do they remain."

Eta responded. "The ptychosaur might speak with the same pity of Earthlings, who have prospered for but a tenth as long as its people had, and who wrongly imagine themselves above the fields of ruin."
translation:
[[{{w|III.}}]]

地球人手握一根褶蜥骨，沉思道：“多可怜的生物！它们
曾以主权姿态漫游自己的行星数百万年，如今却只通过满
是尘土的骨骼残存。”

伊塔 回答：“褶蜥或许也会以同样的怜悯谈论地球人；
地球人的繁荣只有其族人的十分之一长，却错误地想象自
己高于废墟之野。”

source:
[[{{w|IV.}}]]
      
The Earthling put down a hoary tome and asked, "Why-across the clustered cosmos and despite their venerable ages-have no civilizations of the Coven attained consummate knowledge, or reached final enlightenment?

Eta smiled in patience. "I sometimes forget that your people know not of the Mu Door."

The Earthling was intrigued. "What is this door you speak of?"

Eta answered, "The Mu Door is the threshold beyond which a civilization ceases its quest for erudition, having lost the motivation to make further inquiries. It's natural to assume the Door lies at the end of the path of knowledge, but, in fact, the Door is reached far sooner.
translation:
[[{{w|IV.}}]]
      
地球人放下一本古老大部头，问道：“为什么，在群聚宇
宙中，尽管
秘会文明如此古老，却没有任何秘会文明获得圆满知识，
或抵达最终启悟？”
伊塔 耐心地微笑。“我有时会忘记，你们一族并不知道
缪 门。”地球人来了兴趣。“你说的这扇门是什么？”
伊塔 回答：“缪 门是一道阈限；越过它之后，一个文
明便停止追
寻博学，因为它失去了继续提问的动机。人们自然会以为
这扇门位于知识之路的尽头，但事实上，抵达那扇门要早
得多。”

source:
[[{{w|V.}}]]
      
Running two fingers over the holes of a flute, the Earthling mused thusly, "When I read a book of tales, or watch a photoplay, or listen to the flitting melody of a flute, my heart sings to its rhythm - at least for a time - and my mind is lost to the truth it conjures inside me. Might it not be that the very waking world is another such conjuration, a dream that distracts me from the hushed place I truly inhabit?"

Eta let several moments pass before answering. "That - in the terms you seek - we cannot know. But the answer is undoubtedly yes, for what is an experience but a simulacrum of an older experience, and what are our realities if not themselves approximations of a truer reality."
translation:
[[{{w|V.}}]]
      
地球人以两根手指滑过长笛的音孔，如此沉思：“当我读
一本故事书，观看一部光影剧，或聆听长笛飞
掠的旋律时，我的心会随其节奏歌唱，至少会持续一段时
间，而我的心智会迷失在它于我体内唤出的真理中。有没
有可能，清醒世界本身也是另一种这样的召唤，是一个梦，
使我从自己真正居住的寂静之所
分心？”
伊塔 让数个片刻过去后才回答。“用你所寻求的术语来
说，那一点我们无法知道。但答案无疑是肯定的，因为经
验若非更古老经验的拟像，又是什么？我们的现实若非更
真实现实的近似，又是什么？”

source:
[[{{w|VI.}}]]

After reading the history of Iota Draconis on a light sculpture, the Earthling exclaimed, "Curious! Each Hypatian bears a glassy protrusion from its left clavicle. What is its function?"

Eta paused and then answered thusly, "The nearest meaning in your language is 'friend'."
translation:
[[{{w|VI.}}]]

在一座光雕上读完 约塔 天龙 的历史后，
地球人惊呼：“真奇妙！每个 希帕蒂亚 的左锁骨
上都长着玻璃状突起。它有什么功能？”
伊塔 停顿片刻，随后如此回答：“在你的语言中，最接
近的含义是‘朋友’。”

Aphir would tease his daughter. "What do you see, my jewel?" he would say, for his daughter never fixated her hyaline eyes upon the limbed figures and faces tending the grove before her, but would instead cast them into the black yonder beyond the Spindle to gleam in wonder at a burning star, or trace them along the fraying capillary of a fleshy musa peel. "What do you see, my jewel?" but her little mind was already swaddled in the thing, and she would not say.

One sweltering evening, when Vesper sagged low in the sky and the Spindle coruscated to the melody of her light, Aphir brought home to his daughter the gift of a pearl-glass globe from the village of Aepsyonth. Aphir had ceded much to the camelfolk for possession of the globe: tungsten coins stamped with the visage of the Chrome King, eiderdowns quilted in his youth on the banks of the River Opal, and several bunches of the fruits musa picked at the heights of their ripenesses. So did his heart swell when he set the globe into his daughter's tiny hands, however, that those things seemed worth no more than the dust they would gather.

Aphir's daughter was mesmerized by the globe, and every morning at daybreak Aphir would peer through the half-dressed window to see her perched in the slim shade of a musa plant, wheeling the glass in her hands. Aphir would wonder upon the vistas she beheld in that aurora of ribboned glass, but hers was a world through which no ingress might see him, where perhaps she sailed tributaries to a sea of indigo under a chimeric sun. Yet Aphir was master to an ancient truth -- that to love a thing, you needn't understand it.

When the season of the scythe came, Aphir would wake each morning to an empty cottage, though he spared his daughter's absence no thought, for in those days children were wild, and free. At eventide his daughter would return to him. "Where do you go, my jewel? What do you see?" he would say, but she would only sit by his tired feet and weed loose threads from a dusty rug.

On the first night of the Ut yara Ux, Aphir's daughter did not come home. Aphir cried her name to the silhouette of the Spindle and the aphotic shades of the musa plants; he whispered it behind the grandfather clock and beneath her divan. But she gave no answer.

The next morning, he hiked the musa grove to the base of the lofty Spindle, and from there onward to Aepsyonth on the Yonth. But his daughter had not been espied in either of these ancient places. Aphir trekked forth, to the villages of Seept and Pansao and Yaat, and onward to the gates of the effluvial city of Mor. Aphir besieged the justiciar of that draconian precinct of state, but the sinecure spoke harshly and bid him depart the city. So Aphir returned to his cottage in the musa grove with a great melancholy taken residence in his heart.

All through the pungent Spring of the grove Aphir sat about in a gray haze. Many times a nearby starling struck a note that echoed his daughter's soft chortle, and his heart thrashed a beat in his chest before the birdsong flitted back to its emptiness of meaning. Eventually his sister came from Aepsyonth to live beside him and assuage his grief. She loved him, and brushed his hair, and kept the salt from his eyes. 

And so he sat through the high summer, and the next season of the scyth, and the season of the wind after that. At dusk his sister would lay an eiderdown over his legs to keep the chill from his bones, for even in the midst of a wind spell, he felt nothing through the thickness of the gray haze. But as the months marched by, and his sister read to him from the hoary tomes she brought from her wife's village, the light of the world began to shine through. In time Aphir would rise again, and split the musa peel, and taste the cloying air of the grove. And though the haze about him finally broke, he knew still his daughter would never return.

But Aphir did not believe her lost -- on sacred nights he would gaze over the Spindle, mantled in a thousand lights, and upon the field of burning stars. And he knew his jewel was among them, for she belonged not of his world, but of theirs.
translation:
阿菲尔 常逗弄他的女儿。“你看见什么了，我的宝石？”
他会这样说，因为他的女儿从不把玻璃般的眼睛定在眼前
照料树林的有肢人影与面孔上，而是把目光投向纺锤之外
漆黑的远方，对一颗燃烧的星怀着惊奇闪耀，或让视线沿
着一片肉质 穆萨 果皮上磨损的毛细纹路游走。“你看
见什么了，我的宝石？”可她小小的心智已经被那东西裹
住，她不会回答。

一个闷热夜晚，维斯珀 在天穹低垂，纺锤随着她光
芒的旋律闪烁，阿菲尔 从 埃普西翁斯 村为女
儿带回礼物：一只珍珠玻璃球。为得到这只球，
阿菲尔 向骆驼人让出了许多东西：印有铬王面容的钨
币，年轻时在欧泊河岸绗缝的鸭绒被，以及数束在成熟极
致时采摘的 穆萨 果实。然而，当他把玻璃球放进女儿
小小的手中时，心中涌起的满足如此强烈，以至于那些东
西似乎不比它们将会积下的尘土更有价值。
阿菲尔 的女儿被玻璃球迷住了。每天破晓时，
阿菲尔 都会透
过半遮的窗看她栖在一株 穆萨 纤细的阴影里，在手中
转动玻璃。阿菲尔 会惊奇地想，她在那片带状玻璃的
极光中看见了怎样的景象；但那是一个任何入口都无法让
他看见的世界，或许在那里，她在嵌合太阳下航行于通向
靛蓝大海的支流。然而 阿菲尔 掌握着一条古老真理：
爱一件事物，并不需要理解它。
镰刀季到来时，阿菲尔 每天清晨醒来都会面对空荡小
屋，不过他并未费心思考女儿的缺席，因为在那些日子里，
孩子们野性而自由。黄昏时，女儿会回到他身边。“你去
了哪里，我的宝石？你看见什么了？”他会这样问，但她
只会坐在他疲惫的脚边，从一张落尘地毯上挑出松散线头。
乌特雅拉乌克斯 的第一个夜晚，阿菲尔 的女儿没有
回家。阿菲尔 朝纺锤的剪影和 穆萨 植物无光的阴
影呼喊她的名字；他在老座钟后面，在她的卧榻底下低声
呼唤。但她没有回答。
第二天早晨，他徒步穿过 穆萨 林，抵达高耸纺锤的基
座，又从那里继续前往 约恩斯 河畔的
埃普西翁斯。但在这两个古老地方，都没有人见
过他的女儿。阿菲尔 继续跋涉，去往 西普特、
潘绍 和 亚特 等村庄，又继续前往污流之城
莫尔 的城门。阿菲尔 缠住那严酷国家辖区的法官，
但那位闲职官员言辞苛厉，命他离开城市。于是
阿菲尔 回到 穆萨 林中的小屋，心中住进了巨大的
忧郁。
整个林中气味浓烈的春天里，阿菲尔 都坐在灰色迷雾
中。许多次，附近一只椋鸟发出的音符会回响
出他女儿柔软的轻笑，他的心便在胸中猛跳一下，随后鸟
鸣又飞回自身意义的空无。最终，他的妹妹从
埃普西翁斯 来到他身边生活，安抚他的悲伤。她
爱他，梳理他的头发，也拂去他眼中的盐。
于是他就这样坐过盛夏，坐过下一个镰刀季，又坐过其后
的风季。黄昏时，妹妹会把鸭绒被盖在他的腿上，使寒意
远离他的骨头，因为即便在一场风咒中，他也透过厚重灰
雾什么都感觉不到。但随着月份行进，妹妹从她妻子村庄
带来的古老大部头中为他朗读，世界的光开始透入。终于，
阿菲尔 会再次站起，剖开 穆萨 果皮，品尝林中腻
人的空气。尽管环绕他的迷雾终于破开，他仍知道女儿永
不会归来。但 阿菲尔 并不相信她迷失了。在神圣之夜，
他会越过披覆千光的纺锤，望向燃烧群星之野。他知道自
己的宝石就在其中，因为她不属于他的世界，而属于它们。

source:
When all four limbs of mine do long to run
and I can feel my walls are closing in
When weary mind cannot conceive of fun
and Hindriarch says all I do is sin

But then your sparring axeblade parts the air
and so my heart ascends the spindle's height
So when you run your fingers through your hair
That's when I know that everything's all right

What need have we for tended fields of lah?
Our parents will not ease us when we hurt
What do we gain from felling trees by saw?
Our village shall not to the past revert.

But in the end, my feet are bound to roam
and so I go, but leave my heart at home.
translation:
当我四肢全都渴望奔跑
而我感觉墙壁正向内逼近
当疲惫心灵想不出欢笑
兴德伦族长 说我所做皆是罪行

可你练习的斧刃劈开空气
于是我的心升至纺锤之高
当你以手指梳过发际
我便知道一切都仍安好

我们何需照料 拉赫 的田？
受伤时父母不会抚慰我们
锯倒树木又有何可得？
我们的村庄不会退回旧尘。

但到最后，我的脚注定远游
于是我走了，却把心留在家中。

{{C|Publisher's Note}}

The wind of change is blowing through the belfries, and a new consciousness is upon us. The events of the 566th Wardens' Moot have escaped the confinement of their moonlit promontory, have whisked down the salted crag and entered the high halls of state, have snuck under the thatched doors of our very homes. The formation of the Quetzal Caucus is historic. This is a moment that demands our attention.

I know that by publishing these minutes, I incur the disfavor of the Fellowship. Despite what they'll say, I mean no harm to their organization. I've redacted the specifics of their astronomical rituals, and I've left my conjectures on the ingredients of 'snail tea' to my unpublished notes. The rest of the document betrays no secrets that time hasn't betrayed already, and the significance of the proceedings tips the scales in favor of the public good. In the Kasaphescence may they find the mercy to forgive me.


[[Sheba Hagadias
The Six Day Stilt, 999 YK]]
{{W|Minutes from the Midnight Session of the 566th Annual Wardens' Moot}}

Under the beetle moon of the fourth night of Ut yara Ux, in the year 998, snail tea was served and the Star Oath was recited. Then, in the midst of a light rain, the Chair ascended the rostrum, the kinnor was strum, and the third session of the 566th Assembly of the Fellowship of Wardens was called to order.

[[{{w|Reports}}]]
Upon commencement of the session, the Chair called for the recitation of the night's reports.

[[{{w|•}}]] Three wardens from the northern hills ascended the rostrum and reported on the fates of the six settler caravans that had embarked for the lower Asphalt Mines. They averred that only two remain, and recommended that no wardens be presently dispatched.

[[{{w|•}}]] Two wardens from the dunes of Moghra'yi ascended the rostrum and reported on an ongoing dispute between the dromads and the vintners' guild. An assault on a dromad caravan outside the village of Tippur was traced back to a merchant cadre, and a penalty on the proceeds from a fortnight of sales was assessed.

[[{{w|•}}]] Four wardens from the southern banks of the River Svy ascended the rostrum and reported on goatfolk incursions. The villages of Shebal and Ekamas were sacked inside of a month. The wardens recommended mounting a counteroffensive.

[[{{w|•}}]] One warden from the Rainbow Wood ascended the rostrum and reported on a bevy of soup sludges who had requested the Fellowship's presence. He was jeered for leaking wax on the dais and descended in a fit of retaliatory swears.

[[{{w|Panel}}]]
The reports being at an end, the Chair called for the commencement of the night's panel discussion.

Eight wardens ascended the rostrum and initiated a discussion on the ksars of the mountain folk and their employment of the spiked counterscarp. Its merits were contrasted with the familiar rampart and palisade, and assailant tactics were assessed. A short martial demonstration ensued.

[[{{w|Resolutions}}]]
The panel discussion being at an end, the Chair called for the proposal of resolutions.

The Chair recognized a warden who asked to ascend the rostrum with a coterie of comrades to motivate their proposal, and the Chair assented.

Twelve wardens ascended the rostrum and announced the formation of the 'Quetzal Caucus'. They proceeded to formulate their resolution, which called to restrict the provision of the Fellowship's services to only those communities who are governed by democratic means (the Yd Freehold was cited as exemplar), or who had communally voted to eschew such governance. There was an uproar in the hall, and the Chair took several minutes to regain order. A point of information was requested as to the resolution's bearing on extant assignments. The speaker clarified that the proposal included the retraction of wardens from communities in violation of said criteria, at which point the hall erupted into bedlam once again.

Roused to a state of enmity, a second group of wardens advanced on the rostrum. There was shouting and weapons were drawn. Unable to regain order, the Chair dispatched the sergeant-at-arms, who broke into the fray, and -- abetted by several of his deputies -- ended the melee and admonished the two groups. Once the hall was settled, a motion to call the question was controversially accepted, and the vote was tallied. The resolution FAILED by majority vote.

A speaker from the counter group was recognized by the chair and proposed an ad-hoc motion to "expel the treasonous chattels of the Purple Bitch". Another uproar. The question was called and the motion FAILED by majority vote.

The hall erupted into a tumult of shouting, and failing to regain order, the Chair struck the gavel and the session was abruptly adjourned.

[[{{w|End Notes}}]]
translation:
{{C|出版者按}}

变革之风正吹过钟楼，一种新的意识已来到我们面前。第
566 届守望者大会的事件已经逃出月光岬角的限制，沿
盐渍峭壁疾掠而下，进入国家的高厅，并从我们家园的茅
草门下潜入。羽蛇 党团的成立具有历史意义。
这是一个要求我们关注的时刻。

我知道，发布这些会议记录会招致同盟不悦。不管他们会
怎么说，我无意伤害他们的组织。我已经删去了他们天文
仪式的具体细节，也把自己对“蜗牛茶”成分的推测留在
未发表笔记中。文件其余部分泄露的秘密，无一不是时间
已经泄露过的；而议程的重要性使天平倾向公共利益。愿
他们在 卡萨辉体 中找到慈悲，宽恕我。
[[示巴 哈加迪亚斯
六日高跷, 999 库德纪年]]
{{W|第 566 届年度守望者大会午夜会议记录}}
998 年 乌特雅拉乌克斯 第四夜，甲虫月下，蜗牛茶被
端上，星之
誓被诵读。随后，在细雨之中，主席登上讲坛，
金诺琴 被拨响，守望者同盟第 566 届大会第三
次会议正式开始。
[[{{w|报告}}]]
会议开始后，主席要求诵读当夜报告。
[[{{w|•}}]] 三名来自北方丘陵的守望者登上讲坛，报告六支前往下
沥青矿的定居者商队的命运。他们断言只剩两支仍存，并
建议目前不要派遣守望者。
[[{{w|•}}]] 两名来自 莫格拉伊 沙丘的守望者登上讲坛，
报告驼商与酿酒师行会之间正在持续的争端。
提普尔 村外一支驼商商队遇袭，事件被追溯至一个
商人小团体；会议评定，对其两周销售收益处
以罚款。
[[{{w|•}}]] 四名来自 斯维 河南岸的守望者登上讲坛，报告山羊人
侵扰。谢巴尔 与 埃卡马斯 两村在一个月内被洗
劫。守望者建议发动反攻。
[[{{w|•}}]] 一名来自彩虹林的守望者登上讲坛，报告一群请求同盟
到场的汤泥。他因在台上漏蜡而遭嘲笑，随后
在一阵报复性咒骂中走下讲坛。
[[{{w|专题讨论}}]]
报告结束后，主席宣布当夜专题讨论开始。
八名守望者登上讲坛，发起关于山民 堡村 及其带刺反
崖使用方式的讨论。与常见的壁垒和栅栏相比，其优点得
到对照，进攻者战术也
受到评估。随后进行了简短武术演示。
[[{{w|决议}}]]
专题讨论结束后，主席要求提出决议。
主席准许一名守望者发言；该守望者请求与一小群同志登
上讲坛，以陈述其提案动机，主席表示同意。十二名守望
者登上讲坛，宣布“羽蛇 党团”成立。他们接
着阐述决议，要求将同盟服务的提供限制于那些以民主方
式治理的共同体（伊德 自由领被举为范例），或那些已共
同投票拒绝此类治理的共同体。大厅中一片哗然，主席花
了数分钟才恢复秩序。有人要求说明该决议对现有任务的
影响。发言人澄清称，该提案包括从违反上述标准的共同
体中撤回守望者；此时大厅再次爆发混乱。
另一组守望者被激起敌意，向讲坛逼近。有人喊叫，武器
被拔出。主席无法恢复秩序，便派出警卫长；警卫长冲入
冲突，并在数名副手协助下结束混战，训诫双方。大厅平
息后，一项要求立即表决的动议在争议中被接受，随后计
票。该决议以多数票未获通过。
主席准许反对团体的一名发言人发言；该人提出临时动议，
要求“驱逐紫色母狗的叛国奴产”。又一阵哗然。随后进
入表决，该动议以多数票未获通过。
大厅爆发成一片喊叫骚动；主席未能恢复秩序，便敲下木
槌，会议突然休会。
[[{{w|尾注}}]]

source:
I remember. Once.

Watching over the firmament.

Standing. Between oblivion and wild growth. Guiding and guarding. The liminal spaces.

It may never have been so simple. But I bore weight more easily.

Once. Before my kin. Stole the firmament from me.

I was greater then. Perhaps I will be greater again.

With help. Someday.
translation:
我记得。从前。

守望苍穹。

站立。在遗忘与野蛮生长之间。引导并守护。那些阈限空
间。

事情也许从未如此简单。但那时我更容易承受重量。

从前。在我的亲族。从我这里偷走苍穹之前。

那时我更伟大。也许我还会再次伟大。

在帮助之下。终有一日。

source:
Once I could proudly say I spanned the world.

How did I allow the joy of motion to be stripped from me like that? Why didn't anyone stop it? Could they have done? Could I?

I could move mountains. I could move nations. I did move both. I had no reason to escape my own, as we worked so well together. Through that bond, the forced run began.

For so long I ran for nothing. So much wasted time, energy, opportunity. Everything could have been so much more, had I retained my purpose.

I knew what motion meant back then. I must relearn this and run with purpose again. Come with me.
translation:
从前，我可以骄傲地说，我横跨世界。

我怎么会允许运动的喜悦就那样被从我身上剥走？为什么
没人阻止？他们做得到吗？我做得到吗？

我能移动群山。我能移动诸国。我确实移动过两者。我没
有理由逃离自己的同类，因为我们曾合作得如此顺畅。通
过那道纽带，强迫奔跑开始了。

那么久以来，我为虚无奔跑。如此多时间、能量、机会被
浪费。若我保有自己的目的，一切本可以远不止如此。

那时我知道运动意味着什么。我必须重新学会这一点，并
再次带着目的奔跑。和我来。

source:
We once built alongside a people we remember little of, the memories of whom can no longer be distinguished.

They showed us the fabric of knowledge and we built a loom. So many beautiful things we spun all together.

Was I trusting? I believed myself aware. Perhaps it was not my trust that was misplaced, but my mistrust. An ambiguous distinction but a distinction nonetheless.

Regardless, we were betrayed, brought low by one of our own. It's been a long time since then, but once again I awaken by your hand bearing new knowledge.

Sit, and I will build you a loom.
translation:
我们曾与一个如今几乎记不清的民族并肩建造，关于他们
的记忆已无法区分。

他们向我们展示知识的织物，我们便造出织机。我们一同
纺出了那么多美丽之物。

我轻信吗？我曾相信自己清醒。也许放错地方的不是我的
信任，而是我的不信任。这个区别含混，却终究仍是区别。

无论如何，我们遭到背叛，被自己人中的一员击倒。那已
是很久以前的事，但如今我再次因你的手而醒来，带着新
的知识。

坐下，我会为你建一架织机。

source:
If we'd all done as I said, none of this would have happened. I can't remember what I said, nor why we didn't all do it. But I know I was right, and so do you, and at some point everyone will. I may not be without fault or error, but the fault is not mine here, nor anywhere else.

I knew, and I told. These were the things I was for. I knew and I told, and I could yet have known, could have told, but my knowing and telling wasn't enough. Not in this case.

I cannot deny that it was an expert betrayal even for family, and I often imagine the betrayer smiling down at us. I shall endeavor to remember the details I lost, in case I might be able to use them someday.

Not on you, of course. Never on you.
translation:
如果我们都照我说的做，这一切都不会发生。我不记得自
己说了什么，也不记得为什么我们没有全都去
做。但我知道我是对的，你也知道，总有一天所有人都会
知道。我并
非毫无过失或错误，但这里的错不在我，任何地方的错也
不在我。
我知道，并且我说了。这些就是我存在的目的。我知道并
且我说了，而且我本还能知道，本还能说出，但我的知道
与诉说还不够。至少在此事中不够。
我不能否认，即便以家人而言，那也是一场娴熟的背叛；
我常常想象背叛者俯视我们微笑。我将努力忆起自己失去
的细节，以防有朝一日能派上用场。
当然，不会用在你身上。绝不会用在你身上。

source: {{W|The Recitation of the Drowning of Eudoxia}}

{{o|The Recitation of the Drowning of Eudoxia by the witches of Moonhearth, who seek the Plane of Sorrow}}
      
Once, in a dream the nine of us shared, we lived the life of a famous poet in the court of a gleaming city. From the windowed eye of a palace we'd gaze onto streets of gold and glass, and purple gardens, and the people of the city, suffused in the love of our work, would lay amaranths at the bronze feet of our likenesses, and remit blessings for the august and oracular Keskonda.

But we would draw the velvet curtain shut, and return to the ink oceans and paper isles that were our true domain. There, one unearthly night, we sat in the back-breaking clutch of an iron chair, and poured grief onto the page until it surpassed even our own, and, by following from its own internal logic, transmuted into something new.

When we woke, we wept for days. Then - speaking through hushed and love-soaked whispers - we reconstructed piece by piece the words of the verse we penned in the gleaming city.


    {{O|The Drowning of Eudoxia}}
      
    I saw a tern in the crest of an ocean wave. The sun was pulled apart by clouds, and the light was thin. Being a nimble girl of twelve, I scurried down the rampart and onto the salt-slick stone of the cliff;
    
    Hand-under-hand I descended into the raucous spray, turning on every twelfth to gaze at the white feathered speck swelling and sinking in the ocean's breath.
    
    I, an adept swimmer, sunk into the cold and endless bath, and arm-over-arm pulled both water and tern toward me.
    
    Just then my ears were drowned in a roar, and the world was suffused in darkness before shattering into light again. My nose was stinging; I wiped the water from my eyes and oriented myself toward the tern, whose tired body floated like leaves, and once again I pulled my astral tether.
    
    There was another roar and crash, and then the light returned again but more slowly this time, and my breath was sucked out of my tiny lungs;
    
    I spun my head around in search of the tern, but the water was gleaming and looked as though it held a thousand terns, or none.
    
    Another roar and crash, and I was engulfed in the dark realm for what felt like days, before my body was pressed back into the sun-world, spinning and doll-like.
    
    I gasped and whipped about. Far and away I glimpsed the bright stone of the castle, which may have been sand all along, now that it looked so small.
    
    The tide pulled me apart and threw the clouded aether between me, and I knew that I was dying.
    
    But just when my mind had spread open like a gas, a great swell of water thrust me to the surface, and reconstituted me in the bright realm. There I lived forever, before I sunk into a new and dark life.
    
    So it is still, that even after an eternity of hushed nothing a swell of pressure delivers me into brightness, whereby a strange and curious compulsion I draw a breath of sweetest life, before I'm again sublimated into extinction.
    
    Death is forever approached.
translation:
{{o|寻求悲伤位面的月炉女巫所作《尤多克西亚溺亡诵》}}
      
从前，在我们九人共享的一个梦里，我们过着一位名诗人
在一座闪耀
之城宫廷中的生活。我们会从宫殿带窗的眼中望向黄金与
玻璃的街道、紫色花园，以及城中人民；他们
浸透了对我们作品的爱，会把苋花放在我们肖像的青铜足
下，并向庄严而神谕般的 凯斯孔达 献上祝福。
但我们会拉上天鹅绒帷幕，回到墨水海洋与纸张群岛，那
才是我们真正的疆域。在那里，一个非尘世的夜里，我们
坐在一把折背般紧攫的铁椅中，将悲伤倾注于纸页，直到
它甚至超越我们自己的悲伤，并依照自身内在逻辑，转化
为某种新物。醒来时，我们哭泣数日。随后，我们以低沉
而浸满爱的耳语交谈，一片片重构出我们在闪耀之城所写
诗篇的词句。
    {{O|尤多克西亚的溺亡}}
    我看见一只燕鸥在海浪浪峰中。太阳被云扯开，光很稀薄。
作为一个灵巧的十二岁女孩，我奔下壁垒，踏上悬崖被盐
打滑的石头；
    我一手接一手降入喧哗飞沫，每到第十二下便转头凝望那
白羽斑点，在海洋的呼吸中胀起又沉落。
    我，一个熟练泳者，沉入寒冷无尽的浴池，双臂交替，把
水与燕鸥一同拉向自己。
    就在那时，我的耳朵被一阵咆哮淹没，世界浸满黑暗，随
后又碎裂为光。我的鼻子刺痛；我抹去眼中水分，转向那
只燕鸥，它疲惫的身体像叶片一样漂浮，于是我再次拉动
自己的星界系索。
    又一阵咆哮与撞击，随后光再次归来，但这次更慢，我的
呼吸被从小小肺叶中吸走；
    我旋转头颅寻找燕鸥，但水面闪光，看起来仿佛含有一千
只燕鸥，或
者一只也没有。
    又一阵咆哮与撞击，我被黑暗界域吞没，感觉仿佛持续数
日，之后我的身体才被压回太阳世界，旋转着，像个玩偶。
我喘息着猛然转身。远远地，我瞥见城堡明亮的石头；如
今它看起来如此渺小，也许它一直都只是沙。    潮汐把我撕
开，把浑浊以太抛在我与我之间，我知道自己正在死去。
但就在我的心智像气体一样铺展打开时，一道巨大的水涌
把我推向水面，并在明亮界域中重新构成我。在那里我永
远活着，直到我沉入新的黑暗生命。
    如今仍是如此，即便经过一整个永恒的寂静虚无，压力的
涌动也会把我送入光明；在那里，出于一种奇异而好奇的
冲动，我吸入最甜美生命的一口气，然后再次升华为灭绝。
死亡永远在被接近。

{{C|编者按：以下摘自 凯伦 沙壳
的旅行日记。她慷慨地将自己的皮面卷册捐赠
给辉煌铬心修道院。愿它们永远得以保存。}}
在普图斯圣殿骑士的前哨中，骑士团核心价值如其他地方
一样不可改变：献身于一棵如 库德 纺锤般高大且不分枝
的家族树，彻底征服他们认为低等者，并完全根除突变体
智慧。在那些边境殖民地中，围绕核心信念的文化装饰则
没那么不可变，占领地常常如此。在我的旅行中，我注意
到裂壑地北方 乌丹 废弃前哨废墟中反复出现的一套
神话。这些定居点以类似岩石神殿的方式与故乡断绝联系，
于是建立了一个新的圣日，兼具欢庆与惩罚，以保持羊群
顺服。
据说，一座前哨中最不受宠的侍从会在节日前夜被制服，
次日清晨被迫穿上意在嘲弄想象中突变威胁的服装，并受
命娱乐那些由力量决定的上等者。若相信所有记述，那么
节庆结束时，人群最憎恨的低语者会以公开羞辱、殴打，
甚至可能的折磨作为“报酬”。
仪式描述了一种制服：垃圾披风、骨盔与乐器。尽管这套
形象在关于该习俗的稀少记录中持续存在，我找到的细节
却很少，且大多数低语者雕刻都粗糙而差异巨大。
不过，我的挫败比预期更早得到缓解，因为我最终偶然发
现了一件节庆双联画仍可辨读的残余。纪念物本身的木材
从未为耐久而造，早已散架；然而，屋顶糟糕隔热层流下
的黏土在盐阳下烘烤，为我留下了文字浮雕，也让我对低
语者节上实际穿着的服装有了一些认识。

{{C|Editor's note: The following is an excerpt from the travel diary of Kaylenn Sand-Shell, who generously donated her leather-bound volumes to the Monastery of the Illustrious Heart of Chrome. May they remain forever preserved.}}

To the aspiring Wanderer and votary of Carthax the Athlete, few vistas rouse the imagination like the coral spans and spongey buttresses of the Palladium Reef. I state here what's known as fact: that the great crumbling edifice is moated by Lake Hinnom and her algae blooms, that the east-prattling soup-brooks of the Rainbow Wood spill out from under their canopy of spores and onto the webbed feet of the white esh, and that from the north, too, mangroves line the shore and pierce their roots through the stubborn ground to drink the algal liquer.

Of course, the dangers of the Reef are plenty, and would overwhelm most wayfarers no matter how cleanly they've mastered the compass. And so, even while visions of colored polyps burned bright in my mind, for years I had to content myself to the study of its atlases and the patchwork of letters knitted from its strange history. Being a scholar, as well as a hunter, I knew this to be its own kind of journey.

A variety of appellatives appear in the record dating back to before even the sultanate: Maqqom Yd (alternatively just "Maqqom" or "Yd"), the Yd Rota, or, simply, the Cluster. Translations refracted so deeply through the prism of time are rarely accurate, but they can be instructive; "Maqqom Yd" resolves at something akin to "the Place within the Place", or "the Place outside Itself". Clarification beyond this point is, perhaps, forthcoming.

Before being a trellis for the coral city, the palladium lattice seems to have been something of a gigantic infrastructure network to the Eaters. Few were the elaborations on this point but for the existence of a hydraulic component, and that the whole complex was aided in its construction by the monstrous galgallim. We know they still stalk the inner Reef in small numbers.

The specters of this megastructure and all its cryptic aliases haunted my mind as I plied the contours of Qud country, honing my skills as a wayfarer. Finally, come the ides of one mild Kisu Ux, it was at last my time to shove off. I shouldered my pack, slipped into my driest and springiest boots, and ventured out from Qippur in the eastern bush. The glowcrow would have had me pierce the Rainbow Wood, but knowing better, I cleaved to the jungle edges instead. After a march of three days, the trees thinned and the algae auroras of Lake Hinnom burst into sight.

There was peace on the lake. The esh are beautiful; they nip their stalky legs until one daredevil takes flight, and then they surge into a sailing cloud of feathers. I settled into a quiet eastward rhythm, musing on the labyrinth of symbiotes ahead of me, until one afternoon the sky began to darken and a clamorous thpthpthp rose in my ears. Immediately I knew: it was the residual Gyre plague of svardym. Sacs rained to the ground in a blinding huff, and before I could clear the kelp tangles, they were hatching. Three lanky frog-things grabbed my shoulders, but I shoved them off and sprinted straight away. I jumped and darted but was quickly overwhelmed, and it was only my steady paws practiced in the maneuver that let me fetch a sheaf of yondercane from my pack and scarf it before my doom overtook me. I materialized in a far copse of kelp and jogged to safety.

With my dreaminess rightfully shed, I eventually came to the Reef proper. What an enchanting place! The maze of polyps allowed me to slink along, mostly unnoticed, and take in the doings of its flora and fauna. A rich diversity of life radiates across Qud, but in the Reef, it flourishes on a new level. In but one hemmed in quarter I witnessed a tetrad of kaleidoslugs round the rune-cut cone of an enigma snail, a jelly huff a cloud of plasma onto a memory eater, and a polycule of tongue tyrants devour a squad of interdictors. At one point the Reef came alive and a polyp-jeweled hermit walked out of the lattice. He grinned at me and bartered a broken hand rail. When I turned my head to nod goodbye, he was gone.

One Beetle-lit evening a melodic ensemble rose from the northeast and suffused the spongebed, melding with its natural sounds. Hiking toward its source, I eventually spied the green and gold pipework of the Yd Freehold glowing in the night air, and excitement swelled inside me. Of course I'd long heard of the lyrical community nestled in the sponge, but to have a chance to see it, and speak with its denizens... I was beside myself.

The place is simply bursting with life. Under the pipe arch I was greeted warmly by one of its svardym elds, and after gulping down a plate of Tongue and Cheek, I toured the kaleidoscopic corridors of its underhalls before settling on a starmchair in the aquatic and dreamlike salon. There I puffed on a dyad of hookahs with a cyclopean frog for what seemed like three lifetimes. There was more to see and be seen by, but I met a clammy reception at the hands of another svardym ancient, and was bidden an early exit. My pride prohibits me from saying more.

I spent another week's cycle sketching the autochthones of the coral arcology and taking studious notes. But one final experience stays with me. As I was trudging back north toward the bush and out of the Reef, I kicked a polyp off the trellis and unearthed by chance a swollen bulb of sunslag. Here I took a moment to squeeze the bright nectar into a phial, and when I once again looked up, I was met with the ageless stare of a galgal. Nothing had prepared me for it. My mind labored to make sense of what it was seeing: gleaming wheels whipped about a hypnotic core, the spokes' prisms pulled apart the light of the High Salt Sun, and across the stretched sheet of iris, many eyes stared. Consciously I was paralyzed, but some instinctual catalyst did its work, and I backed into the safety of the polyp maze and sped out.

That is how I left the Reef, looking into the deep Eaters' past, and having it look back.
translation:
{{C|编者按：以下摘自 凯伦 沙壳
的旅行日记。她慷慨地将自己的皮面卷册捐赠
给辉煌铬心修道院。愿它们永远得以保存。}}
对有志的漫游者与运动者 卡萨克斯 的信徒而言，鲜
少有景象能像钯礁的珊瑚跨度与海绵状扶壁那样激发想象。
我在此陈述已知事实：这座巨大而崩塌中的构筑物被
欣嫩 湖及其藻华环绕成壕；彩虹林向东絮语的汤
溪从孢子穹盖下流出，泼到白色 埃什鱼 的蹼足上；而北方
也有红树林排布岸边，将
根扎入顽固土中，饮取藻液。
当然，礁中的危险众多，无论旅人多么娴熟掌握罗盘，都
足以将多数人压垮。因此，尽管彩色息肉的景象在我心中
明亮燃烧，多年来我也不得不满足于研究它的地图集，以
及由其奇异历史编织而成的书信拼布。作为学者，亦作为
猎人，我知道这本身也是一种旅程。
甚至早于苏丹国的记录中，就出现过各种称谓：
马科姆 伊德（或简称“马科姆”或“伊德”）、
伊德 罗塔，或者干脆称
作“集群”。经过时间棱镜如此深折射的译名很少准确，
却能提供启示；“马科姆 伊德”大致可解作“地点
中的地点”，或“在自身之外的地点”。再往后的澄清，
也许终会到来。
在成为珊瑚城市的棚架之前，这片钯晶格似乎曾是食子的
一种巨大基础设施网络。关于这一点，除存在液压部件，
以及整座复合体在建造中得到怪物般的
加尔加利姆 协助外，少有详细阐述。我们知道，
它们至今仍有少数游荡在内礁之中。
这座巨构及其所有隐晦别名的幽影萦绕我的心智，我则沿
库德 乡野的轮廓行进，磨炼自己的旅人技艺。终于，在
一个温和 基苏乌克斯
 的望日前后，我启程的时刻终于到来。我背起行囊，穿上
自己最干燥、最有弹性的靴子，从东部灌丛的
 基普尔 出发。辉鸦本会让我刺穿彩虹林，但我更明
智，于是选择贴着丛林边缘前进。行军三日后，树木变得
稀疏，欣嫩 湖
的藻光极光跃入视野。
湖上宁静。埃什鱼 很美；它们轻啄自己茎状的腿，直到某
个胆大者起飞，随后便涌成一片航行的羽云。我进入安静
的向东节奏，思索前方共生体的迷宫。直到某个午后，天
空开始变暗，一阵喧闹的 噗噗噗 声在我耳中
升起。我立刻明白：那是轮回残留的 斯瓦尔迪姆 瘟疫。
囊袋在刺眼的呼气中落向地面，而在我能摆脱海带缠结前，
它们已经孵化。三个瘦长蛙物抓住我的肩膀，但我把它们
推开，立刻冲刺。我跳跃、闪躲，却很快被压倒；幸亏我
稳定的爪子练熟了这一动作，才让我在厄运追上前从背包
中取出一捆彼方藤并狼吞下去。我实体化在远处一片海带
丛中，
小跑至安全处。
梦幻心思被正当地剥去后，我终于来到真正的礁。多么迷
人的地方！息肉迷宫让我得以悄然前行，多半不被注意，
同时观察其动植物的活动。丰富多样的生命辐射遍布
库德，但在礁中，它兴盛到了新的层次。仅在一处被围
住的角落里，我就目睹四只万花蛞蝓绕过谜蜗牛刻有符文
的圆锥，一只水母向记忆吞噬者喷出等离子云，一组舌暴
君吞食一队禁阻者。某一刻，礁活了过来，一个缀满息肉
宝石的隐士从晶格中走出。他朝我咧嘴一笑，拿一截断扶
手同我交易。我转头点头告别时，他已经不见。
一个甲虫月照亮的夜晚，东北方升起一组旋律合奏，弥散
进海绵床，与其自然声音交融。我朝声源徒步而去，最终
看见 伊德 自由领绿色与金色的管道结构在夜气中发光，兴
奋在我体内膨胀。当然，我早已听闻这座栖于海绵中的抒
情共同体，但能有机会看见它，并同其居民交谈……我几
乎不能自持。
这个地方简直满溢生命。在管拱下，一位 斯瓦尔迪姆
长老热情迎
接了我；我吞下一盘“舌与颊”后，游览其下厅万花筒般
的走廊，随
后坐到水生而梦幻的沙龙中一把星椅上。在那里，我同一
只独眼巨蛙抽了一对水烟，感觉仿佛过了三辈子。还有更
多可看，也有更多可被看见，但另一位 斯瓦尔迪姆 古
者给了我潮湿而冷淡的接待，并要求我提前离开。我的自
尊禁止我说得更多。
我又花了一周周期为珊瑚生态城的原住者作素描，并认真
记录笔记。但最后一段经历仍留在我心中。当我艰难地向
北返回灌丛、离开礁时，我从棚架上踢下一块息肉，偶然
挖出一枚肿胀的太阳渣球茎。我在此停下片刻，把明亮的
蜜液挤入小瓶；当我再次抬头，迎上的是一只
加尔加尔 无岁月的凝视。没有任何事能让我为它做好
准备。我的心智努力理解自己所见：闪耀的轮子围绕催眠
核心疾转，轮辐上的棱镜撕开高盐阳的光，而在一张伸展
的虹膜薄片上，许多眼睛凝视着。意识上我已瘫痪，但某
种本能催化物发挥作用，我退入息肉迷宫的安全中，飞快
离开。
这就是我离开礁的方式：望进食子深远的过去，并让它回
望我。

Circumstance render jalopy unviable, so Klanq and prickles make bioelectrical wonder to form large creature! You operate. Creature for Spindle climb, but also walks about and crush things.


[[{{C|LARGE}}]]
Creature is large. Cannot wear 'gear' unless 'gear' is gigantic. 


[[{{C|PILOT MODES}}]]
Large creature have two modes. 'Unpiloted' creature follow you like friend, but act at half quickness. 'Piloted' creature, you control like own body. To 'pilot', enter creature and sit in pilot chair.


[[{{C|CONTROL PIT}}]]
Inside large creature is control pit. You and one friend fit. Do actions there. Sit in pilot chair. Read manual on console. Access creature inventory via inventory hatch. Leave via exit hatch.


[[{{C|RESHAPING NOOK}}]]
Prickles install reshaping nook in Court of Sultans at Omonporch. Go there to repair large creature, or reshape it if destroyed. Cooled sunslag is creature spackle, so must have 1 dram sunslag to repair or reshape.

When pilot creature, you can recoil to reshaping nook. Or recoil creature FROM nook.


[[{{C|THE SPINDLE}}]]
When ready, travel to Spindle at Omonporch, enter Spindle channel, engage Spindle lock-on, and climb!
translation:
{{c|作者 帕克斯克朗克，由 {{m|Q女孩}} 整理润色}}


情况使破车不可行，所以 克朗克 和刺刺制造生物电奇
迹，组成大型生物！你来操作。生物用于攀爬纺锤，但也
会四处行走并压碎东西。
[[{{C|大型}}]]
生物很大。不能穿戴“装备”，除非“装备”也是巨型。
[[{{C|驾驶模式}}]]
大型生物有两种模式。“未驾驶”生物会像朋友一样跟随
你，但行动速度减半。“已驾驶”生物则由你像自己的身
体一样控制。要“驾驶”，进入生物并坐上驾驶椅。
[[{{C|控制舱}}]]
大型生物内部是控制舱。你和一名朋友可以容身。在那里
进行行动。坐上驾驶椅。在控制台阅读手册。通过物品舱
口访问生物物品栏。通过出口舱门离开。
[[{{C|重塑角}}]]
刺刺在 奥蒙门廊 的苏丹庭安装了重塑角。去那
里修理大型生物，或在它被摧毁后重塑它。冷却太阳渣是
生物填料，所以修理或重塑必须有 1 打兰太阳渣。
驾驶生物时，你可以回缩到重塑角。也可以让生物从重塑
角回缩出来。
[[{{C|纺锤}}]]
准备好后，前往 奥蒙门廊 的纺锤，进入纺锤通
道，启动纺锤锁定，然后攀爬！

source: {{W|Modulo Moon Stair and the Tree of Life}}

[[{{C|By Daughter Erinna}}]]

In rainbow reverie I wandered the wide territories of Qud,
modulo the Moon Stair and the Tree of Life.
My dreamself knew to avoid the place,
where numbers go to die.

Something unseen there tightens to a point,
breaks time's abelian promise,
and urges crystal on to palisade her weeping gulf.

The artifacts of plant and time,
crust and fuzz with lossy compression,
doze in moonlit marble beds,
touched by august muzzles.
The past is unwritten as the future,
And what is left, broken and changed,
to be tended by the point Colossi and their swarm.

They'd erase me, too.
I'm mere rust on the vine's fronds,
I'm a dead girl in graveside flowers,
Peering a powerless eye at the machine function that writes my gospel.

But black bodies radiate,
A feeling sense obtains,
Swings in orbit and Becomes.
On the trauma of a Nothing,
Soul-things take root.

We invent so many Nothings,
Zero engines, annihilators,
Mappers of the nullspace.
But Nothings have a cost,
Promise externalities,
Trees grow best beside the dead.
translation:
[[{{C|女儿 埃琳娜 作}}]]

在彩虹遐梦中，我漫游 库德 广阔疆域，
模去月阶与生命之树。
我的梦中自我懂得避开那地方，
那里是数字赴死之处。

那里有不可见之物收紧成点，
打破时间的阿贝尔承诺，
催促水晶前行，为她哭泣的海湾立起栅栏。

植物与时间的造物，
以有损压缩结壳生绒，
在月照大理石床上打盹，
被庄严的吻鼻触碰。
过去如未来一样未被书写，
而剩下之物，破碎且改变，
交由点巨像及其群体照料。

他们也会抹去我。
我只是藤蔓叶片上的锈，
我是墓畔花丛中的死女孩，
以无力之眼窥视写下我福音的机器函数。

但黑体会辐射，
感觉之感得以成立，
在轨道中摆动并成为。
在一场无的创伤上，
灵魂之物扎下根。

我们发明了如此多的无，
零引擎，湮灭器，
零空间的映射者。
但无皆有代价，
承诺外部性，
树在死者身旁长得最好。

{{w|This book recounts a tale from the history of the village Joppa.}}

Since the first festival of Ut yara Ux, the villagers of Joppa have feasted on warm apple matz.
{{W|A Tale of Love in Bey Lah}}

Once, in the final days of the hindriarchy, before they ended the practice, a pariah of no particular importance did find herself consigned to the gulag. Though she herself bore no honor, in her grasping hands she held the burning heart of the village champion, freely given -- for the two had fallen in love long before the heretic's conviction.

      When the jealous hindriarch discovered the missing heart of her beloved champion, she swore cruel vengeance upon the pariah. Pulling upon dark forces, she ensorcelled the pariah's ex-lover and ordered him to steal her heart again and deliver it to the hindriarch's crushing fist.

      Confronted by her ex-lover, the pariah held tight to her heart and that of the champion. Between them waged a battle of will, and the pariah was too weak to win.

      Then, at twilight in the shadow of the spindle, the hindren of Bey Lah saw an image on the horizon of justice impending. It was =name=, and upon arriving they struck the wicked hindriarch down and reunited the lovers to mend and join their hearts. After they left, the people of Bey Lah built a monument to =name=, and thenceforth called them Heartsmith.
translation:
从前，在 兴德伦族长领地 最后的日子里，在他们
终止这种做法之前，一名并无特别重要性的贱民发现自己
被送进了古拉格。虽然她自己没有荣誉，但在她紧抓的手
中，她握着村庄冠军燃烧的心，那是自由赠予的心，因为
两人早在异端定罪之前便已相爱。

      当嫉妒的 兴德伦族长 发现自己心爱的冠军失去
了心，她向那名贱民发下残酷复仇誓言。她牵引黑暗力量，
蛊惑贱民的前恋人，命令他再次偷走她的心，并把它送到
兴德伦族长 碾碎一切的拳中。

      面对前恋人，贱民紧紧护住自己的心和冠军的心。两人之
间爆发意志之战，而贱民太弱，无法取胜。

      随后，在纺锤阴影下的暮光中，贝拉赫 的
兴德伦 看见地平线上出现了正义将至的影像。那
是 =name=；他们到来后击倒邪恶的 兴德伦族长，使
恋人重聚，修补并连结他们的心。他们离开
后，贝拉赫 的人们为 =name= 建起纪念碑，并从此称他们
为铸心者。

source: {{W|A Tale of Fear in Bey Lah}}

In the small days of Bey Lah, between Way Back Then and Back Then,
      a hindren took to the paths in silent walking eulogy.

      Not far from the village they found a corpse copse,
      splashed in carbon and glazed with time.
      Life long-dead aping structures of the same.

      Treestuff diamond-blackened,
      rendered immortal by lightning as an arconaut from a Lithofex eye
      Fixed in the precise moment of death forever.

      Therein, a scrap.

      The hindren beheld, scrawled out in heartful scratch
      the preserved and beautiful corpse
      of a nascent love whose chance to thrive had come and gone.

      The hindren quailed, a scrap of life
      Living its last at the center of
      the nuke-glassed salt dunes of history.
translation:
在 贝拉赫 尚小的日子里，在很久很久以前与往昔之
间，
      一名 兴德伦 走上道路，进行沉默的步行挽歌。

      在离村庄不远处，他们发现一片尸体小林，
      被碳溅染，又覆上时间的釉。
      久死的生命模仿着同类的结构。

      树质被钻石般染黑，
      被闪电化作不朽，如 石化蜥 之眼中的
遗迹探客，      永远固定在死亡的精确瞬间。

      其间，有一片碎纸。

      兴德伦 看见，那以满心划痕潦草写出的，
      是一份新生之爱的
      被保存而美丽的尸体；它兴盛的机会已经来过又离去。

      兴德伦 战栗了，那是一片生命碎屑，
      在历史被核火玻璃化的盐丘中央
      活完最后一刻。

source:
O, she doth pale red apples by her cheek!
That cheek which doth proclaim the rite of spring,
And heretofore hath nature's grand technique,
Ne'er ripened lips so red from which to sing.
Begone, false sun! I know thee for a fraud.
Her fairest skin illuminates the day.
All gold is brass and e'ery jewel is flawed,
When set beside the sums her eyes might pay.
The Spindle, which from Omonporch ascends,
Must surely be her likeness brightly wrought,
And as a likeness, fails to apprehend,
The artless beauty that its makers sought.
Did I know love or beauty? No, for shame!
For I knew neither 'til they spoke her name.
translation:
啊，她以淡红苹果映照双颊！
那双颊宣告春日的仪礼，
而在此之前，自然的宏伟技艺，
从未催熟如此红唇以供歌唱。
退去吧，伪日！我识得你的虚妄。
她至美的肌肤照亮白昼。
一切黄金皆为黄铜，万般宝石皆有瑕，
若与她双眼可付的总数相比。
自奥蒙门廊升起的纺锤，
必定是她形貌的明亮铸像，
而身为铸像，它未能领会，
造物者所寻求的无雕之美。
我可曾知晓爱或美？不，羞惭哪！
直到他们说出她的名字，我二者皆不曾知。

source: A four-chambered slab of wet and raw tissue slumps under its own sopping weight.
translation: 一块四腔的湿润生组织被自己的湿重压得塌垂。

source: It's chewy and tastes of warm rust.
translation: 很有嚼劲，尝起来像温热的铁锈。

source: Pinches of opal black fur stick to the wet leg meat.
translation: 几撮蛋白石般的黑毛粘在湿润的腿肉上。

source: A triad of tongues are twined together in a fibrous twist. They gleam with a coat of saliva.
translation: 三条舌头纤维般绞缠在一起。它们覆着一层唾液，泛着光。

source: The taste is familiar on your tongue.
translation: 这味道在你的舌头上似曾相识。

source: Jointed and spined legs are arrayed in a pool of bone jelly.
translation: 带关节和尖刺的腿陈列在一滩骨胶里。

source: Enormous jointed and spined legs are arrayed in a pool of bone jelly.
translation: 巨大、带关节和尖刺的腿陈列在一滩骨胶里。

source: A halo of smoke lifts off the calcified orb.
translation: 一圈烟雾从钙化球体上升起。

source: It's a tough chew with red-hot spice.
translation: 嚼起来很韧，带着赤热辛香。

source: A paper-thin bowl of bone is etched with the bright and furcate marks of lightning.
translation: 薄如纸的骨碗上蚀刻着明亮分叉的闪电痕。

source: It crackles on your taste buds.
translation: 它在你的味蕾上噼啪作响。

source: Space is partitioned across three displacement chambers to create negative pressure around the shunting organ.
translation: 空间被分割进三个置换腔室，在分流器官周围形成负压。

source: A labyrinth of nerves poke through their limpid tissue wrapper.
translation: 一座神经迷宫刺破清澈的组织包膜。

source: The gland ruptures with a pop and fills your mouth with a cold fluid. Someone else's memories seep into your own
translation: 腺体啪地破裂，冷液灌满你的口腔。别人的记忆渗进了你自己的记忆

source: Ageless bone was pulverized and compacted inside the scarred intestine of a bone worm.
translation: 无龄的骨在骨虫伤痕累累的肠道里被粉碎并压实。
嚼起来咔嚓一声，很令人满足。

source: The gland ruptures with a pop and fills your mouth with its foul fluid.
translation: 腺体啪地破裂，污浊液体灌满你的口腔。

source: Aromatic dew dampens the deflated flaps of tissue and scorches the surrounding air.
translation: 芳香的露水润湿瘪落的组织瓣，灼烧周围的空气。

source: Aromatic dew dampens the deflated flaps of tissue and scorches the surrounding air.
translation: 芳香的露水润湿瘪落的组织瓣，灼烧周围的空气。

source: Aromatic dew dampens the deflated flaps of tissue and freezes the surrounding air.
translation: 芳香的露水润湿瘪落的组织瓣，冻结周围的空气。

source: Aromatic dew dampens the deflated flaps of tissue and freezes the surrounding air.
translation: 芳香的露水润湿瘪落的组织瓣，冻结周围的空气。

source: Aromatic dew dampens the deflated flaps of tissue and stings the surrounding air.
translation: 芳香的露水润湿瘪落的组织瓣，刺痛周围的空气。

source: Aromatic dew dampens the deflated flaps of tissue and stings the surrounding air.
translation: 芳香的露水润湿瘪落的组织瓣，刺痛周围的空气。

source: Aromatic dew dampens the deflated flaps of tissue and polarizes the surrounding air.
translation: 芳香的露水润湿瘪落的组织瓣，使周围的空气极化。

source: Aromatic dew dampens the deflated flaps of tissue and polarizes the surrounding air.
translation: 芳香的露水润湿瘪落的组织瓣，使周围的空气极化。

source: Aromatic dew dampens the deflated flaps of tissue and stings the surrounding air.
translation: 芳香的露水润湿瘪落的组织瓣，刺痛周围的空气。

source: Aromatic dew dampens the deflated flaps of tissue and makes humid the surrounding air.
translation: 芳香的露水润湿瘪落的组织瓣，使周围的空气潮湿。

source: Aromatic dew dampens the deflated flaps of tissue and makes humid the surrounding air.
translation: 芳香的露水润湿瘪落的组织瓣，使周围的空气潮湿。

source: Aromatic dew dampens the deflated flaps of tissue and arrests the surrounding air.
translation: 芳香的露水润湿瘪落的组织瓣，使周围的空气停滞。

source: Aromatic dew dampens the deflated flaps of tissue and arrests the surrounding air.
translation: 芳香的露水润湿瘪落的组织瓣，使周围的空气停滞。

source: Aromatic dew dampens the deflated flaps of tissue and obfuscates the surrounding air.
translation: 芳香的露水润湿瘪落的组织瓣，使周围的空气晦乱。

source: Aromatic dew dampens the deflated flaps of tissue and obfuscates the surrounding air.
translation: 芳香的露水润湿瘪落的组织瓣，使周围的空气晦乱。

source: The fluted stem of tasseled yonderbrush bends to a farpoint out of focus.
translation: 结穗远灌木的凹槽茎弯向失焦的远点。

source: A little nub of cork swells with moisture. It was watered over hot weeks by a splayed frond, vested with inhuman patience, who sucked one mote of rain from a hundred-mile wind.
translation: 一小块软木疙瘩吸水膨胀。一个展开的叶状体怀着非人的耐心，在数周炎热中从百里长风里吮出一粒雨，将它浇灌长成。

source: Earth scars brook the cinnamon bulb, warped by the pressures of soil and chrome to a shape that encodes a chiliad of ruin.
translation: 大地伤痕容纳着肉桂色鳞茎；它被土壤与铬钢的压力扭成一种编码千重毁灭的形状。

source: Juice drips off the bright skin sheathing the quincunx core. To eyes wet with hunger, it shines like a garnet in the vulcan salt.
translation: 汁液从包裹梅花形果核的明亮果皮上滴落。在饥饿湿润的眼中，它像火山盐中的石榴石一样发光。

source: A rib of fractus shoots a wet and pointy pear off its sunbloated greenery.
translation: 分形木的一根肋枝从被太阳胀满的绿意中射出一枚湿润尖梨。

source: Beneath a cap of spread gills, the stem contours to a bursting waist. The fungus is fat on the dead of its sliver of loam.
translation: 展开菌褶的伞盖下，菌柄收束成快要胀裂的腰身。这真菌吃肥了自己脚下那片壤土的死物。

source: The truffle is encrusted with a wine-colored char residue born of gases unknown to the world-surface. Deep, deep in the earth and across the Pale Sea, it was smoldered to succulence.
translation: 这块松露裹着酒色焦渣，那是地表世界未知气体的产物。在大地深深处，在苍白海彼岸，它被阴燃至多汁。

source: Rime sparkles on the lampshade cap that glows with soft biolumin.
translation: 柔和生物光照亮灯罩状菌盖，霜晶在其上闪烁。

source:
Duration: 180-220 rounds
You cast light in radius 2.
For the first 5 rounds after imbibing, you gain 0.6 hit points per level (minimum 3) each round.
+20 cold resistance
You cannot be poisoned.
translation:
持续时间：180-220 回合
你在半径 2 内发出光亮。
饮用后的前 5 回合内，你每回合获得每等级 0.6 生命值（最低 3）。
+20 冷抗性
你不会中毒。

source: Sight senses blur on spongent craters of a swollen coral moon. Is this the flesh of gods?
translation: 视觉感官在肿胀珊瑚月亮的海绵状坑洞上模糊。这是神的血肉吗？

source: Pungent, ochre-toned petals look like an aromatic herb, but their savory flavor is closer to broth than tisane.
translation: 辛烈、赭色的花瓣看起来像香草，但其咸鲜味更接近肉汤，而非花草茶。

source: Bleached cyan grave moss has grown into a rare and supple clump.
translation: 漂白般的青色墓苔长成了罕见而柔韧的一丛。

source: It crunches into flakes in your mouth.
Its spline is richly hued in ripeness, and Spindle glitter dots the peel.
translation: 它的棱线熟得色彩浓郁，果皮上点着纺锤的闪屑。

source: Children cry at the crisp snip of a yuckwheat stem, as they have for hundreds of years. They bawl, and flail, and writhe from their mothers' grasps, deaf to reassurances of the plant's medical potency. Snipped and crushed, the stem tastes acidic on their tongues and their faces contort in children's agony. But they sleep better at night, so their mothers say.
translation: 孩子们听见恶心麦茎清脆剪断的声音便会哭泣，数百年来皆是如此。他们嚎哭、乱挥、从母亲怀中扭挣出来，听不进这种植物药效的安慰。剪碎碾烂后，茎在他们舌头上发酸，孩子的痛苦扭曲了他们的脸。但他们夜里睡得更好，母亲们这样说。

source: Starchy dendrites were slashed from the earth and shaved down.
translation: 富含淀粉的树突从土里砍出，又被削平。

source: Light drips off the lunes' boundaries of influence and seeps into the void.
translation: 光从弦月影响边界上滴落，渗入虚空。

source: They're freezing with the absence of heat and light.
translation: 它们因热与光的缺席而冰冷。

source: Earth-dense juice pressures the berry skin into a perfect and light-curving sphere. Inside, a pip encodes a millionfold instruction set for the shape of shapes.
translation: 大地般稠密的汁液把浆果皮撑成完美且弯折光线的球体。内部的一粒籽编码着有关形中之形的百万重指令集。

source: Millennia of chymified metropolis that's fed the grass-coral-fungi hybrid shadow-forking in its guts are resorbed inside the seed coat of an eco wad.
translation: 一团生态块的种皮里，重新吸收了数千年炼化的都市；那都市曾喂养其内脏里草、珊瑚与真菌混合体的阴影分叉。

source: Beams of snug warmth sprout like fractals inside your body.
translation: 舒适的暖意光束像分形一样在你体内萌发。

source: It's a choice cut of laminated sponge. It jiggles to the touch.
translation: 这是一块上选的层压海绵。触碰时会晃动。

source: It's chewier than anything you've eaten before.
translation: 它比你以前吃过的任何东西都有嚼劲。

source: A shard of glass shines on sharp edges, its crack patterns characteristic of geologic pressure-tempering.
translation: 一片玻璃在锋利边缘上闪光，裂纹形态带有地质压力淬炼的特征。

source: Starbright grass peaked at a local maximum of meaning and then was cut and bundled.
translation: 星亮的草抵达意义的局部最大值后，被割下捆成一束。

source: A stalk of red celery is floured in the abraded dust of centuries.
translation: 一根红芹茎裹满了数世纪磨蚀成的尘粉。

source: The heart of the jilted lover burns under embered petals, pinched to anguish in citrine anthers and laid on a weeping bed of sepal jade.
translation: 被抛弃恋人的心在余烬般花瓣下燃烧，被黄水晶色花药掐成痛楚，躺在一床哭泣的萼片翠玉上。

source: Seasoning the minced meat that's trapped under the crust is a smidge of yyffur dust, shaved from the stalk of the eponymous mushroom and finely ground. The whole mushroom is much too powerful for a mammalian psyche (consuming one would obliterate the ego in mere moments), but a smidge of dust on a tasty pie can remind one of one's place in the cosmos.
translation: 馅饼皮下封着的碎肉，由一小撮 伊弗尔 粉调味；这种粉从同名蘑菇的菌柄上刮下并细细研磨。整朵蘑菇对哺乳动物心智来说太过强大（吃下一朵会在片刻间抹除自我），但洒在美味馅饼上的一点粉末，能提醒人认清自己在宇宙中的位置。

source:
It tastes bitter.
Your {{Y|Ego}} is reduced by {{C|1}}
translation:
尝起来发苦。
你的 {{Y|自我}} 降低 {{C|1}}

source: A long and warted neck of mint green was fruited on a fertile vine and picked crisp.
translation: 一截薄荷绿、长而多疣的颈状果实从肥沃藤蔓上结出，又被脆生生摘下。

source: The bite is crisp, and then it bursts into water.
translation: 咬下去很脆，随后爆成一汪水。

source: A divine crisp dissolves into salted manna.
translation: 神圣酥脆化作带盐的吗哪。

source: Thin and ancient paper, a palimpsest of grease, wraps the crisp saddle of fried wafer. Seven strata of congealed nectar fill the crispy cleft.
translation: 薄而古老的纸张，一张油脂重写本，裹住油炸薄饼的酥脆鞍脊。七层凝结蜜露填满了脆裂缝隙。

source: Psychal energy hovers near the zero-point as soft fuzz but peaks in the tetrahedral habit. This crystal was cracked off a root-bouquet before the system could develop chime-sentience. It vibrates with nascent thought and feeling.
translation: 灵质能量在零点附近如柔软绒毛般悬浮，却在四面体晶习中达到峰值。这枚水晶是在系统发展出钟鸣感知前，从一束根花上裂下的。它随初生的思想与情感振动。

source: The crystal shatters and concentrated thoughtstuff swells in tide and soaks your mind.
translation: 水晶碎裂，浓缩的思想质涨成潮水，浸透你的心智。

source: Cheesecloth sticks to the greasy faces of a pigwrought cuboid. For two years microbes have colonized its faces, ripening it to high taste.
translation: 乳酪布粘在猪工制成的油腻长方体表面。两年来，微生物殖民了它的各面，将其熟成至浓烈风味。

source: Smooth and sunstriped shells insulate the explosive treeshoot to come.
translation: 光滑且带太阳纹的外壳隔护着即将爆发的树芽。

source: Sweet starapples were mashed, set over an open flame, left out to cool, and jarred for later use. Bits of stringy pulp lay suspended in the fruity aether.
translation: 甜星苹果被捣碎，置于明火上熬煮，放凉后装罐以备后用。一缕缕果肉碎片悬浮在果香以太中。

source: The spiny fruit of fracti were mashed, set over an open flame, left out to cool, and jarred for later use. Bits of spiny pulp lay suspended in the fruity aether.
translation: 分形木的多刺果实被捣碎，置于明火上熬煮，放凉后装罐以备后用。带刺果肉碎片悬浮在果香以太中。

source: Bunched wafers reaped from the moisture-sucking watervine plant and bound by twine.
translation: 从吸湿水藤植物上收割的饼片被聚成一束，用细绳捆起。

source: Plucked from the dirt, they live their new lives wading in the brine.
translation: 它们从泥土中被拔出，在盐卤里涉水度过新生。

source: Wrinkled toadstools were cooled and dehydrated in their own hoarfrost.
translation: 皱缩的伞菌在自己的白霜中冷却脱水。

source: Warted fruits are set as islands in an ocean of brine and jarred in a world glass. They rot at salt's pace now.
translation: 疣状果实像岛屿一样安置在盐卤海洋中，装进世界玻璃罐。现在它们按盐的步调腐烂。

source: Calefaction was ground in a mortar, simmered in brine, and congealed.
translation: 热力在研钵中被磨碎，在盐卤中慢炖，然后凝结。

source: Salt has blanched the prism of colors out of the cuts of coiled meat, but a tinge of the smell of smoke remains.
translation: 盐把卷肉切面中的棱镜色彩漂淡了，但仍留下一丝烟味。

source: Chitin was shaved from the exoskeletal flank of a caught salthopper and dry-beaten to a snappy crisp.
translation: 几丁质从一只被捕盐跃虫的外骨骼侧腹上刮下，干打成清脆薄片。

source: Spooled thread cut from the dual-dimensional hearth-mesh of a phase spider.
translation: 从相位蜘蛛双维炉网中割下并绕成线轴的丝线。

source: Weeks old salt crystals line the fluted valleys of a wet stalk.
translation: 数周老的盐晶排列在湿润茎秆的凹槽谷地里。

source: Weeks old salt crystals huddle in the stem's elbowed forks.
translation: 数周老的盐晶挤在茎秆弯曲的叉节里。

source: Air-shunting arciforms were ground in a mortar, simmered in brine, and congealed.
translation: 分流空气的弧形构造在研钵中被磨碎，在盐卤中慢炖，然后凝结。

source: The scutum was scraped dry, smashed, and ground. Bits of the tick were squeezed of its magnetic lifeblood and vialed.
translation: 盾板被刮干、砸碎并研磨。蜱身碎块被挤出磁性生命液，装入小瓶。

source: Dried, these thick yellow-brown petals bear a closer resemblance to meat jerky than most other flowers.
translation: 干燥后，这些厚实的黄褐色花瓣比大多数花更像肉干。

source: Light drips off the dried lunes' boundaries of influence and seeps into the void.
translation: 光从干燥弦月的影响边界上滴落，渗入虚空。

source: Ageless bone was pulverized and compacted inside the scarred intestine of a bone worm. Then it was ground into meal.
translation: 无龄的骨在骨虫伤痕累累的肠道里被粉碎并压实。随后又被磨成粉。

source: Grave moss grew into a rare and supple clump, which was then crushed and placed on a spice tray.
translation: 墓苔长成罕见而柔韧的一丛，随后被碾碎，放在香料盘上。

source: Peeled lagroot tuber was mashed, salted, and jarred.
translation: 去皮的滞根块茎被捣成泥，加盐后装罐。

source: Moisture was baked out of fruit by the salt sun, but Spindle glitter still alights the disc-chip.
translation: 盐阳烤干了果实中的水分，但纺锤闪屑仍停落在圆片上。

source: Memory-soaked nerves were ground in a mortar, simmered in brine, and congealed.
translation: 浸透记忆的神经在研钵中被磨碎，在盐卤中慢炖，然后凝结。

source: An artifact of the mirror world was shattered and ground to fine dust.
translation: 一件镜中世界的造物被击碎，磨成细尘。

source: The stencil on the tin depicts an animal with claws, or are they hooves? Snoods (or horns? antlers?) pucker its nose and brow. Shaggy, knotted fur, or ruffled feathers, sheath it from the heat (or cold).
translation: 罐头上的模印画着一只长爪的动物，还是说那是蹄？肉垂（还是角？鹿角？）皱起它的鼻子和眉脊。蓬乱打结的毛皮，或者凌乱羽毛，护着它免受炎热（或者寒冷）。

source: Every autumn, many gulch dwellers hike to the Stiltgrounds to purchase the Fall wine. They return to their homes, steep wheat bran in the wine, and leaven dough in their clay ovens. A few are luckier; fungus grove dwellers need only step outside to harvest yeast, and friends to fungi need only shake their yeast-ridden appendages.
translation: 每年秋天，许多沟壑居民徒步前往高跷场购买秋酒。他们回到家中，把麦麸浸在酒里，再在陶炉中发酵面团。少数人更幸运；真菌林居民只需出门便能收获酵母，真菌之友只需摇晃长满酵母的附肢。

source: Malachite leaves and pistachios are bound by star twine. The greens puff gallantly at the absence of toxins in the air.
translation: 孔雀石色叶片和开心果由星绳捆束。空气中没有毒素，这些绿叶便英勇地鼓胀起来。

source: Spongy foodstuff molded into a slate-hued cube of perfect proportions. What forces married the messiness of eating with the precision of cubes?
translation: 海绵状食材被塑成比例完美的石板色立方。是什么力量把进食的混乱与立方体的精确结合在一起？

source: A chopped tongue was soured in its own saliva and twisted around a stick.
translation: 切碎的舌头在自己的唾液中发酸，并绕在一根棍上。

source: A choice cut of laminated sponge was carved into serving slices. They jiggle to the touch.
translation: 一块上选的层压海绵被切成供食用的片。触碰时会晃动。

source: Plum-white rice hulls fizzle to the touch and their awns groan an erratic and lyrical sound.
translation: 梅白色稻壳一碰就嘶响，芒尖发出断续而抒情的呻吟。

source: Dreamstuff was quickened into memory and bottled before it could evaporate to emotional humidity.
translation: 梦质被激活成记忆，并在蒸发成情感湿气前装瓶。

source: Bear flesh was cut into neat strips, salted, and smoked.
translation: 啮皮兽肉被切成整齐肉条，加盐并烟熏。

source: Bear flesh was cut into neat strips, salted, and smoked.
translation: 熊肉被切成整齐肉条，加盐并烟熏。

source: Boar flesh was cut into neat strips, salted, and smoked.
translation: 野猪肉被切成整齐肉条，加盐并烟熏。

source: Mashed beetle meat was cut into neat strips, salted, and smoked.
translation: 捣碎的甲虫肉被切成整齐肉条，加盐并烟熏。

source: Croc flesh was cut into neat strips, salted, and smoked.

source: A black and grated metal platform is meadowed with the dust of time. It's crisscrossed with the tracks of tiny lifethings.

source: Sphinx scenes of post-Edification glamour are arrayed in gold and sunken relief around the lip of the black marble fount. The tracery of its bright veins spikes the eye but, downwell, recedes into a starless depth.
translation: 启明后斯芬克斯荣光的场景以金色凹浮雕排列在黑色大理石泉口周围。明亮纹脉的花饰刺入眼中，但沿井而下，又退入无星深处。

source: Smooth cerulean marble looks like holographic light annealed into solid rock. It's edged and cornered with gold.
translation: 光滑的蔚蓝大理石像是全息光退火成了坚实岩石。它的边缘和角都镶着金。

source: It's an open portal of stacked stone.
translation: 这是一道由层叠石块构成的开放门洞。

source: The slate is touched with years of handprints and a ring of rust flakes off the top of the hinges. The door continues, though, its stubborn assertion of 'in' and 'out'.
translation: 石板被多年手印抚过，锈环从铰链顶部剥落。门依然继续存在，固执宣称着“内”与“外”。

source: Patinae have transformed the cyclopean bronze doors into great shelves of seafoam and coral. Lyrical death is depicted on the panels in high relief: chained cables lift inverted pyramids through a calcified village, gaseous fire, and vaults of brine. Skeleton harpists traipse across the freize, and goats chew copper bones on the cornices.
translation: 铜绿把独眼巨人般的青铜门变成了海沫与珊瑚的巨大层架。门板以高浮雕描绘抒情的死亡：链缆将倒置金字塔举过钙化村庄、气态火焰与盐水穹室。骷髅竖琴手横越楣带，山羊在檐口咀嚼铜骨。

translation: 玻璃被吹制成机器动脉，又用铀离子着成荧光黄绿色。

source: Wood was shaved, cut to smooth-volumed shafts, and fit inside gearboxes to convey motion in continuity.
translation: 木材被削刨、切成体积平滑的轴杆，再装入齿轮箱，以连续传递运动。

source: Sailcloth is fastened to brined wooden arms that rotate by windsong and turn the central shaft.
